farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّآ أُخْفِيَ﴾: everyone gives the yāʾ a fatḥa, because it is a past verb, just as you say: أُهلِك الظالمون (the wrongdoers were destroyed).
Ḥamza read it (مَّآ أُخْفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ) with the yāʾ left quiescent [Translator's note: i.e. أُخْفِي, "I conceal"; the vowelling printed in the source quotation shows a fatḥa]. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (مَّآ نُخْفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ} ("what We conceal for them"), and this is a corroboration and support for Ḥamza. Both are correct. If you say ﴿أُخْفِيَ لَهُم﴾ and take (ما) in the sense of (أى) ("which?"), then (ما) is nominative as the deputy agent of a verb whose agent is not named. Whoever reads ﴿أُخْفِيَ لَهُم﴾ with the yāʾ quiescent and takes (ما) in the sense of (أىّ), it is accusative [as object] of ﴿أُخْفِى﴾ and ﴿نُخْفِى﴾. Whoever treats it as equivalent to "the thing" [i.e. as a relative noun, "that which"] makes (تَعْلَمُ) act upon it, so it is accusative in every one of the readings. It has also been read (قُرَّاتِ أعْيُن) (plural, "delights of the eyes"); this is reported from Abū Hurayra.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقاً لاَّ يَسْتَوُونَ﴾: He did not say يستويان (the two are not equal, in the dual), because it is general; when two are not aimed at specifically [as particular individuals], they are treated like a plural. You say in ordinary speech: ما جعل الله المسلم كالكافر فلا تَسوِّيَنَّ بينهم (Allah has not made the Muslim like the unbeliever, so do not make them [plural] equal) — and بينهما (them two). Both are correct.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to me from Manṣūr from Ibrāhīm or from Mujāhid — al-Farrāʾ was unsure — about His saying ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾; he said: misfortunes that befall them in this world, short of Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْ﴾: the readers all have ﴿لَمَّا صَبَرُواْ﴾ with a doubled mīm and fatḥa on the lām. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (بما صَبَروا) (because they were patient), and al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza read it (لِما صَبَروا) on that basis. The position of (ما) is genitive (khafḍ) when the lām has a kasra. When the lām has a fatḥa and [the mīm] is doubled, it has no grammatical position; it is merely a particle.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا﴾: (كَمْ) is in the position of a nominative, through (يَهْدِ), as though you said: "Have the destroyed generations not guided them?" In the reading of ʿAbdullāh in Sūrat Ṭā Hā it is (أَوَلَمْ يَهد لهم مَنْ أهلكنا) ("Has it not guided them, those whom We destroyed?"). (كَم) may also be in the position of an accusative through أَهلكنا while carrying the meaning of a nominative; it is then like your saying: سواءُ عَلىّ أزيداً ضربت أم عمراً (it is the same to me whether you struck Zayd or ʿAmr), where you make (سواء) nominative by interpretation.
And you say: قد تبيّن لى أقام زيد أم عمرو (it has become clear to me whether Zayd or ʿAmr stood), so the clause is nominative in meaning, as if you had said: تبيَّن لى ذاك (that became clear to me).

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْجُرُزِ﴾: al-juruz is land in which there is no vegetation. It is said of a she-camel إنها لجُرَاز when she eats everything, and of a person إنه لجَرُوز when he is a glutton, and a sword is جُرَاز when it leaves nothing without cutting it. One says أرض جُرُز and جُرْز, and أرْض جَرَز and جَرْزٌ — the latter of the Banū Tamīm; each of them, had it been read so, would have been good. It is like البُخُل، البُخْل، البَخَل and البَخْل (miserliness); and الرُغب، الرهب and الشغل each have four forms like that.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَتْحِ﴾: meaning the conquest of Mecca. ﴿لاَ يَنفَعُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِيَمَانُهُمْ﴾: this was mentioned with regard to those of the Banū Kināna whom Khālid ibn al-Walīd killed on that day. They said: "We have become Muslims." Khālid said: "If you have become Muslims, lay down your weapons," and they did so; when they had laid them down, he slaughtered them heavily, because they had previously killed ʿAwf, the father of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and a grandfather of Khālid: al-Mughīra. If ﴿يوم الفتح﴾ were made nominative following the beginning of the speech — because in His saying ﴿مَتَى هذا الفتح﴾ (مَتى) is in the position of a nominative [Translator's note: the apodosis of this conditional is missing in the source; presumably "it would be correct"] — but the proper construction is for ﴿مَتَى﴾ to be in the position of an accusative, and that is more common.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾: he says: He made it good and rendered it beautiful. It is also read (أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُ); Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it so, as though he said: He inspired His creation [with] everything they need. So "the creation" [Translator's note: in this reading] are in the accusative by the verb that falls on (كلّ), as though you said: He taught them everything and made them good [at it]. "Creation" may also be accusative as His saying ﴿أَمْراً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا﴾ is accusative, in many similar instances in the Quran — as though you said: everything, as a creation from Him and an initiation of favours.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ضَلَلْنَا﴾ and ﴿ضَلِلْنا﴾ are two dialectal forms. It has been mentioned from al-Ḥasan and others that he read ﴿إذا صَلِلنا﴾, and it was even attributed to ʿAlī: ﴿صَلِلنا﴾ with ṣād. I do not know it, unless it is a dialect we have not heard. The Arabs only say: "ṣalla al-laḥmu, fa-huwa yaṣillu" (the meat went off), and "aṣalla yuṣillu", and "khamma yakhimmu" and "akhamma yukhimmu". Al-Farrāʾ said: had it been ṣalalnā with fatḥa on the lām, it would be correct, but I do not know it with kasra.
The meaning of ﴿إذا ضَلَلْنا فى الأرْضِ﴾: he says: when our flesh and bones have become dust like the earth. You say: "the water has become lost (ḍalla) in the milk", and "a thing has become lost in a thing" when it hides it and overwhelms it.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «تنزيل»: mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «لا ريب فيه» is parenthetical, and the preposition «من رب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, for digression (iḍrāb). The clause «يقولون» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «هو الحق». The preposition «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «الحق». The interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "He sent it down so that you may warn". The clause «ما أتاهم» is a naʿt of «قوما»; «نذير» is the fāʿil (agent), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «من قبلك» is attached to a naʿt of «نذير». The clause «لعلهم يهتدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «الله»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective). «بينهما»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause). The preposition «في ستة» is attached to «خلق». The clause «ما لكم من دونه من ولي» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «الله»; «وليّ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «لكم» is attached to the khabar, and the preposition «من دونه» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ولي».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «يدبر» is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) {اللَّهُ}. The clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوم». The preposition «ممَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «سنة».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «الذي»: fourth khabar (predicate). The clause «خلقه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كل». The preposition «من طين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بدأ».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «من سلالة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object, and the preposition «من ماء» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «سلالة».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل». «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «تشكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «وقالوا» is resumptive. «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis, "we will be raised". The clause «أئنا لفي خلق جديد» is explicative of the implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "we will be raised". The clause «بل هم كافرون» is resumptive, and the preposition «بلقاء» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ترجعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يتوفَّاكم».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «ولو ترى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {قُلْ}, and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, i.e. "you would have seen a dreadful thing". The clause «المجرمون ناكسو» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «إذ»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ترى»; the past adverb was used here because the seeing is certain to occur. The vocative clause with its response is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied "saying", and this saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "saying: our Lord". The clause «إنَّا موقنون» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «ولو شئنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَلَوْ تَرَى}. The clause «ولكن حق القول» is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "but I did not will that, so it became due". The clause «لأملأنَّ» is the response to the oath, and the oath with its response is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl). «أجمعين»: tawkīd (emphasis) of الناس, genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «فذوقوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding content of speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the object of «ذوقوا» is omitted, i.e. "the punishment". The bāʾ is a preposition and «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ذوقوا». «هذا»: a demonstrative, naʿt (adjective) of «يومكم», interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "the one pointed to". The clause «إنا نسيناكم» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «إنما»: the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa), having no governing effect. «الذين»: fāʿil (agent), and the conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause). «سُجَّدًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «خَرُّوا». The preposition «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from the wāw. The clause «وهم لا يستكبرون» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «سبَّحوا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «تتجافى جنوبهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «سبَّحوا», and the clause «يَدْعُون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جنوبهم». «خوفا»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The clause «ينفقون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يدعون».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «فلا تعلم» is resumptive. The preposition «من قرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». «جزاء»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the preposition «بما» is attached to the maṣdar (جزاء).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The fāʾ is resumptive. «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «كَمَنْ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) its implied khabar (predicate). The clause «لا يستوون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «فلهم جنات» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; «أمَّا» is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl). «نزلا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جنات». The bāʾ is a preposition of causation, «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, and the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نزلا».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «فمأواهم النار» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين». «كلَّ»: an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعيدوا». «ما» is maṣdariyya and temporal, the maṣdar «أن يخرجوا» is the object of أراد, and the interpreted maṣdar «ما أرادوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the implied form is "they will be returned into it at every time of their wanting". The clause «أعيدوا» is resumptive, and the clause «وقيل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أعيدوا». «الذي»: naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «لنذيقنهم» is the response to the oath, and the oath with its response is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَقِيلَ}. «دون»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نذيق». The clause «لعلهم يرجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «ومن أظلم» is resumptive; «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The preposition «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم». The clause «إنا من المجرمين منتقمون» is resumptive, and the preposition «من المجرمين» is attached to the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «فلا تكن» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «آتينا», and «الكتاب» is the second object. The preposition «مِنْ لقائه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مرية», and the preposition «لبني» is attached to a naʿt of «هدى».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «يهدون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أئمة». The clause «لمَّا صبروا» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The preposition «بآياتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يوقنون».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «هو يفصل» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». The preposition «فيما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَفْصِل», and the preposition «فيه» is attached to «يختلفون».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The wāw is resumptive. «يهد» means "become clear", and the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the implied destroying. «كم» is the declarative (khabariyya) one, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. The preposition «من قبلهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أهلكنا», and the preposition «من القرون» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كم». The clause «يمشون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القرون. The clause «كم أهلكنا» explains the implied fāʿil. The clause «أفلا يسمعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «أولم يروا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ}. The interpreted maṣdar «أنَّا نسوق» is the object of «رأى». The clause «تأكل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «زرعا». The clause «أفلا يبصرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «ويقولون» is resumptive. «متى»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هذا». «الفتح»: badal (substitute). The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفع». «إيمانهم»: fāʿil (agent) of «ينفع». The clause «ولا هم ينظرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا ينفع».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «فأعرض» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنهم منتظرون».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, exalted is He, {تَنْزِيل الْكتاب}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and {لَا ريب فِيهِ} is the khabar (predicate). (It may also be nominative) by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a sending down", or "what is recited is a sending down", or "these letters are a sending down" — {الم} indicates the mention of the letters. In ordinary speech the accusative is permissible as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also permissible for {لَا ريب فِيهِ} to be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب, with {من رب الْعَالمين} as the khabar, and this is the best of them; من is then attached to the omitted khabar. If you make {لَا ريب فِيهِ} the khabar, من is attached to تنزيل.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {أم يَقُولُونَ افتراه}: أم here is for moving from one statement to another. It is also said that it has the meaning of بل.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {أحسن كل شَيْء خلقه}: whoever reads the lām in خلقه vowelless makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying {أحسن كل شَيْء} indicates "He created everything with a creating"; so it is like {صنع الله} and {كتاب الله عَلَيْكُم}. It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) for كل. It is also said that it is a second object, with أحسن meaning "made understand" (أفهم), so it takes two objects. In ordinary speech خلقُه is permissible in the nominative, in the sense "that is His creation". Whoever reads it with fatḥa on the lām makes it a past verb, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of كل, or in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of شيء.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {أئذا ضللنا فِي الأَرْض}: the governor of إذا is an implied verb, its implied form being "will we be resurrected when we have vanished and perished in the earth?".

mekki-muskil:16-16.t:
His saying {تَتَجَافَى جنُوبهم}: تتجافى is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in {خروا}. Likewise {يدعونَ} is in the position of a ḥāl, likewise {سجدا}, likewise the position of {وهم لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ}, and likewise the position of {وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفقُونَ}: all of them are aḥwāl from the latent pronoun in خروا and in سجدا. It is also good for each ḥāl after another to be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the ḥāl before it; its like has been discussed before.
His saying {خوفًا وَطَمَعًا}: two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose); it is also said: two maṣdars (verbal nouns).
[Translator's note: the source places the analysis of {خروا}, {سجدا} and {وهم لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ} (32:15) together with 32:16 as written.]

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying مَا أُخْفِي لَهُم: whoever reads the yāʾ vowelless makes the alif the alif of the speaker (first person), and the yāʾ should properly have ḍamma since it is an imperfect verb, but it was made vowelless for lightness. Whoever reads the yāʾ with fatḥa makes it a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), containing a pronoun that stands in place of the agent. As for ما, if you make it have the meaning of الذي, it is in the position of the accusative by تعلم, and the hāʾ is omitted from the ṣila (relative clause) in the reading of whoever makes the yāʾ vowelless, i.e. "(what) I conceal for them". There is no omission in the reading of whoever reads the yāʾ with fatḥa, because the nominative pronoun in أخفي, whose agent is not named, refers to الذي. If you make ما interrogative, it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the reading of whoever reads the yāʾ with fatḥa, and in the position of the accusative by أخفي in the reading of whoever makes the yāʾ vowelless; and the whole clause is in the position of the accusative by تعلم, filling the place of its two objects.
His saying فَلَا تكن فِي مرية من لِقَائِه: the hāʾ refers to الكتاب. He annexed the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object, like His saying, exalted is He, {بسؤال نعجتك}; its implied form is "of Moses' meeting the Book", so Moses was left implied since he had been mentioned before, and the maṣdar was annexed to الكتاب. The hāʾ may also refer to Moses, peace be upon him, so that He has annexed the maṣdar to its agent, with the direct object omitted, as in His saying {لَا يسمعوا دعاءكم}, i.e. your calling them, and as in His saying {لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم}, its implied form being "Allah's hatred of you is greater than your hatred of yourselves". It is also said that the hāʾ refers to what Moses met with, i.e. "so do not be in doubt about meeting what Moses, peace be upon him, met with from his people of harm and denial". It is also said that it refers to Moses without implying any omitted object, i.e. "do not be in doubt, O Muhammad, that you will meet Moses, peace be upon him", because the Prophet ﷺ met Moses, peace be upon him, on the night of the Night Journey (al-isrāʾ). It is also said that the hāʾ refers to Moses and the object is omitted, namely the Torah, i.e. "so do not be in doubt about Moses' receiving the Torah".
[Translator's note: the passage on {فَلَا تكن فِي مرية من لِقَائِه} concerns 32:23; the source places it in this entry.]

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {كلما أَرَادوا}: كلما is an adverb (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying {أولم يهد لَهُم كم أهلكنا}: the fāʿil (agent) of يهد is its maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "has not the guidance guided them?"; this is the view of al-Mubarrad. Al-Farrāʾ said: كم is the agent of يهد. This is not permissible according to the Basrans, because كم is not governed by what precedes it, since in a statement it is in the same standing as in a question: it has the head of the sentence (ṣadr al-kalām), so what precedes it does not govern it, just as what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. It is also said that the agent of يهد is Allah, exalted be His mention, its implied form being "has Allah not guided them?". Whoever reads نهد with the nūn, the agent is Allah, exalted is He, without difficulty or disagreement; this is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Qatāda. كم, according to the Basrans, is in this verse in the position of the accusative by أهلكنا.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هَذَا الْفَتْح}: متى is in the position of the accusative as an adverb, and it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), which is هذا; الفتح is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). متى may also be in the position of the nominative by assuming an omission with هذا, its implied form being "when is the time of this victory?".

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾: the discussion of the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين﴾: تنزيل: mubtadaʾ (subject); الكتاب: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); لا: the lā of generic negation; ريب: the noun of لا; فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of لا; the clause ﴿لا ريب فيه﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب; من رب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; العالمين: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿أم يقولون افتراه﴾: أم is a disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction, so it means "rather" (بل) plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: "Rather, do they say he invented it?" (بل أيقولون افتراه), the hamza being for disapproving interrogation; or ﴿أم﴾ is connective (muttaṣila), in which case a clause must be supplied for the balance (taʿādul) to be sound, the implied form being: "Do they acknowledge it, or do they say: he invented it?" (أيقرون به أم يقولون: افتراه؟). The clause افتراه is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). يقولون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); افتراه: a past verb, the hāʾ being mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he".
﴿بل هو الحق من ربك﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb); هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الحق: khabar (predicate); ﴿من ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الحق.
﴿لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك﴾: the lām is causal (lām al-taʿlīl); تنذر: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an optionally concealed أن after the causal lām; the concealed أن and the imperfect verb form an interpreted maṣdar, genitive (majrūr) by the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, i.e. "We sent it down so that you may warn" (أنزلناه لتنذر). The fāʿil of تنذر is latent, implied as "you"; قومًا: the first mafʿūl bihi, and the second object is omitted, the implied form being "so that you may warn a people of the punishment" (لتنذر قومًا العقاب); ما: negative; أتاهم: a past verb, the pronoun being mafʿūl bihi; مِن: a preposition that is ṣila (i.e. redundant); نذير: genitive in form, nominative in position as fāʿil; the clause ﴿ما أتاهم من نذير﴾ is an adjective of قومًا; من قبلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of نذير.
﴿لعلهم يهتدون﴾: لعل: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿يهتدون﴾ is the khabar of لعل; the clause of hoping is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of لتنذر, i.e. "that you may warn them, hoping for their guidance" (لتنذرهم راجيًا اهتداءهم).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام﴾: the word of majesty (Allah) is mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿خلق...﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position. السماوات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). الأرض: conjoined to السماوات, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿ما﴾: also conjoined to السماوات. بينهما: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. في ستة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خلق; أيام: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ثم استوى على العرش﴾: ثم: a conjunction; استوى: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "he", referring to Allah, glorified and exalted is He; على العرش: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استوى.
﴿ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع﴾: ما: negative; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar; من دونه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial), the hāʾ being muḍāf ilayhi; من: a preposition that is ṣila (i.e. redundant); ولي: genitive in form, nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is for emphasising the negation; شفيع: conjoined to ولي.
﴿أفلا تتذكرون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Do you not hear these admonitions and then not take heed of them?" (ألا تسمعون هذه المواعظ فلا تتذكرون بها) or "Do you hear these admonitions and then not take heed of them?" (أتسمعون هذه المواعظ فلا تتذكرون بها). لا: negative; تتذكرون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض﴾: يدبر: a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); الأمر: the object of يدبر; من السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدبر﴾; إلى الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدبر﴾; the clause ﴿يدبر﴾ is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿الله﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون﴾: ثم: a conjunction; يعرج: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "he"; إليه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرج﴾; في يوم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرج﴾; كان: a defective, abrogating verb (kāna and its sisters); مقداره: the noun of كان, the hāʾ being muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ألف: the khabar of كان; سنة: muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿كان مقداره ألف سنة﴾ is an adjective of يوم; مما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of ﴿ألف﴾ or of ﴿سنة﴾; the clause ﴿تعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); عالم: a first khabar (predicate); الغيب: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the wāw is a conjunction; الشهادة: conjoined to الغيب; العزيز: a second khabar; الرحيم: a third khabar.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه﴾: الذي: a fourth khabar (predicate) or a naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿أحسن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. كل: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); شيء: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); خلقه: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he", and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿خلقه﴾ is an adjective of ﴿شيء﴾, in the position of genitive.
﴿وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; بدأ: a past verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; خلق: mafʿūl bihi; الإنسان: muḍāf ilayhi; من طين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلْق﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين﴾: ثم: a conjunction for sequence with delay; جعل: a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to Allah the Exalted; نسله: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the hāʾ being muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من سلالة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل or to a second object of جعل; من ماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of سلالة; مهين: an adjective of ماء.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة﴾: ثم: a conjunction for sequence and delay; سواه: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); نفخ: conjoined to سواه; فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نفخ; من روحه: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to نفخ; the wāw is a conjunction; جعل: a verb and a latent fāʿil; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل or to a second object of جعل; السمع: mafʿūl bihi; الأبصار والأفئدة: both conjoined to السمع.
﴿قليلا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you give little thanks" (تشكرون شكرا قليلا).
﴿ما﴾: ṣila (i.e. redundant), for emphasising the smallness.
﴿تشكرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿قليلا ما تشكرون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وقالوا أئذا ضللنا في الأرض أئنا لفي خلق جديد﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; إذا: an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the implied form being: "When we are lost in the earth, shall we be resurrected?" (أئذا ضللنا في الأرض نُبعَث). The clause ﴿ضللنا﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ضللنا. أئنا: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; إنّ: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في خلق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; جديد: an adjective of خلق; the clause ﴿وقالوا أئذا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb); هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); بلقاء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كافرون; ربهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; كافرون: the khabar of هم.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون﴾: قل: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; يتوفاكم: an imperfect verb, the kāf being a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ملك: fāʿil; الموت: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الذي: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ملك﴾; وُكِّل: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent, implied as "he"; بكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وُكِّل﴾; the clause ﴿وُكِّل بكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position. ثم: a conjunction with delay; إلى ربكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ترجعون, the pronoun being muḍāf ilayhi; ترجعون: an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw of the plural is the nāʾib fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لو: conditional; ترى: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; إذ: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترى﴾; المجرمون: mubtadaʾ (subject); ناكسو: khabar (predicate), and it is an active participle annexed to its object ﴿رءوسهم﴾; عند ربهم: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ربهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿ترى﴾ here is complete (tāmma), taking no object, i.e. "if seeing were to occur on your part", or its object is omitted, the mubtadaʾ making its mention unnecessary, i.e. "and if you were to see the criminals" (ولو ترى المجرمين). The apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being: "you would have seen a dreadful matter" (لرأيت أمر فظيعا). [Translator's note: the source writes أمر; the accusative أمرًا is expected.]
﴿ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون﴾: ربنا: ﴿رب﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb) because it is annexed, and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the vocative particle being omitted; أبصرنا: a verb and its fāʿil, the object omitted; the clause ﴿أبصرنا﴾ is the response to the vocative, with no grammatical position; سمعنا: a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause ﴿سمعنا﴾ is conjoined to the response to the vocative, with no grammatical position. فارجعنا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ارجعنا: a verb of supplication, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ارجعنا﴾ is conjoined to the response to the vocative, with no grammatical position; نعمل: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request; صالحا: mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نعمل﴾, or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "he did a righteous deed" (عمل عملًا صالحًا). [Translator's note: the source's paraphrase uses عمل; نعمل عملًا صالحًا would match the verse.] إنا موقنون: إنّ is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), ﴿نا﴾ its noun, and موقنون its khabar.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لو: conditional; شئنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); لآتينا: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; آتينا: a verb and its fāʿil; كل: the first object of آتينا; نفس: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); هداها: the second object of آتينا.
﴿ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن: a particle of rectification (istidrāk); حق القول: a verb and its fāʿil; مني: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القول. لأملأن: the lām is in the response to an implied oath; أملأن: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "I"; جهنم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الجنة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أملأن﴾; الناس: conjoined to الجنة; أجمعين: tawkīd (emphasis).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (faṣīḥa), conjoining to something implied, i.e. "it will be said to them: you abandoned faith, so taste!" (قيل لهم تركتم الإيمان فذوقوا). ذوقوا: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); بما: the bāʾ is a preposition of causation, and ما is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar); نسيتم: a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ and the verb ﴿نسيتم﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ذوقوا. The object of ﴿ذوقوا﴾ is omitted, implied as "the punishment" (العذاب); لقاء: the object of نسيتم; يومكم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); هذا: an adjective of يومكم.
﴿إنا نسيناكم﴾: إنّ: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; نسيناكم: a verb, its fāʿil and object; the clause ﴿نسيناكم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
﴿وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ذوقوا: an imperative verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; عذاب: the object of ذوقوا; الخلد: muḍāf ilayhi; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ذوقوا; كنتم: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the tāʾ being its noun; the clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position. إنما: the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; يؤمن: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); بآيتنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمن﴾; الذين: fāʿil (agent); إذا: an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿ذكروا﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the wāw of the plural is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); بها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ذكروا; خروا: a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause ﴿خروا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا; سجدا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of خروا.
﴿وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; سبحوا: a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause ﴿سبحوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿خروا﴾; بحمد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of ﴿سبحوا﴾, i.e. "accompanied by His praise" (ملتبسين بحمده); ربهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿لا يستكبرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate), and the clause ﴿وهم لا يستكبرون﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع﴾: تتجافى: an imperfect verb; جنوبهم: fāʿil (agent); عن المضاجع: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تتجافى; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
﴿يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا﴾: the clause ﴿يدعون﴾ is either resumptive, with no grammatical position, or likewise circumstantial; يدعون ربهم: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿خوفا﴾: two ḥāls (circumstantials), or else two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of an omitted verb, or else two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose); طمعا: conjoined to خوفا.
﴿ومما رزقناهم ينفقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; مما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينفقون; رزقناهم: a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿رزقناهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. ينفقون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا: negative; تعلم نفس: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ما: a relative noun, the object of تعلم; أخفي: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" [Translator's note: in the reading of Ḥafṣ, أُخْفِيَ is a passive past verb; the source calls it imperfect. Translated as written.]; من قرة أعين: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ما; جزاء: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of requital", or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are requited with a requital" (يجزون جزاء). بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جزاء﴾; كانوا: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the wāw of the plural being its noun; the clause ﴿يعملون﴾: its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction; من: mubtadaʾ (subject); كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, the noun of كان being latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; مؤمنا: the khabar (predicate) of كان; the clause ﴿كان مؤمنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. كمن: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and ﴿مَن﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); كان: a defective verb, its noun latent, implied as "he"; فاسقا: the khabar of كان; the clause ﴿كان فاسقا﴾ is the ṣila of the second مَن, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا يستوون﴾: لا: negative; يستوون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون﴾: أما: a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); الذين: mubtadaʾ (subject); آمنوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. عملوا: a verb and its fāʿil; الصالحات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿عملوا الصالحات﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila clause. فلهم: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لهم: a fronted khabar (predicate); جنات: a postponed mubtadaʾ; المأوى: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نزلا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جنات المأوى; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of ﴿نزلا﴾; ما: maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar) or relative; كانوا: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the wāw of the plural being its noun; the clause ﴿يعملون﴾: its khabar.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أما: conditional, for detailing (tafṣīl); الذين: mubtadaʾ (subject); فسقوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿فسقوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); مأواهم: mubtadaʾ; النار: the khabar (predicate) of مأواهم; the clause ﴿مأواهم النار﴾ is the khabar of الذين.
﴿كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها﴾: ﴿كلما﴾: ﴿كلَّ﴾ stands in for an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعيدوا﴾, containing the sense of condition, and ﴿ما﴾ is temporal maṣdariyya; the clause ﴿أرادوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative ﴿ما﴾, and ﴿ما﴾ with what it governs is an interpreted maṣdar, genitive by annexation, the implied form being "every wanting" (كلَّ إرادة), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "every time of their wanting to come out" (كلَّ وقتِ إرادةٍ منهم للخروج). Or ﴿ما﴾ is an indefinite noun qualified by what follows, meaning ﴿وقت﴾ ("time"), with the referring pronoun omitted, the implied form being "every time in which they wanted to come out of it" (كلَّ وقتٍ أرادوا فيه أن يخرجوا منها), so the clause ﴿أرادوا﴾ is in the position of genitive as an adjective of ﴿ما﴾. ﴿أرادوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; أن: maṣdariyya; يخرجوا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنْ﴾ and what follows it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أرادوا﴾, i.e. "whenever they wanted to come out of it" (كلما أرادوا الخروجَ منها). منها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يخرجوا; أعيدوا: a past verb, passive, and the wāw of the plural is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أعيدوا; the clause ﴿أعيدوا﴾ is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position.
﴿وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause ﴿قيل﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أعيدوا﴾; لهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قيل; ذوقوا: a verb and its fāʿil; عذاب: mafʿūl bihi; النار: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿ذوقوا عذاب النار...﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); الذي: an adjective of عذاب; كنتم: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the tāʾ being its noun; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تكذبون; the clause ﴿تكذبون﴾ is the khabar of كنتم. The clause ﴿كنتم به تكذبون﴾ is the ṣila of الذي, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is in the response to an implied oath; نذيقنهم: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "we"; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm the sign of the plural. من العذاب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نذيقنهم; الأدنى: an adjective of العذاب; دون: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿نذيق﴾; العذاب: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الأكبر: an adjective; لعلهم: لعل is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters) expressing hope, and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿يرجعون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لعل.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); أظلم: khabar (predicate); ممن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم; the clause ﴿ذُكِّر﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of مَن, with no grammatical position. بآيات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ذُكِّر; ربه: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ثم: a conjunction with delay; أعرض: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أعرض﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ذُكِّر﴾; عنها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أعرض; the clause ﴿ومن أظلم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنا من المجرمين منتقمون﴾: إنّ: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; من المجرمين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to منتقمون; منتقمون: the khabar of إنّ.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the response to the omitted oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); آتينا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); موسى: the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتينا; الكتاب: the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (faṣīḥa); لا: prohibitive; تكن: a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the noun of تكن being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you"; في مرية: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; من لقائه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of مرية.
﴿وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلناه: a verb, its fāʿil and the first mafʿūl bihi; هدى: the second mafʿūl bihi; لبني: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿هدى﴾ or to an adjective of ﴿هدى﴾; إسرائيل: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause ﴿جعلنا﴾ is conjoined to the first ﴿جعلنا﴾; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as the second object of ﴿جعلنا﴾; أئمة: the first object of ﴿جعلنا﴾; the clause ﴿يهدون﴾ is an adjective of أئمة; بأمرنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يهدون; لما: an adverb meaning "when" (حين), attached to جعلنا, and the apodosis of لما is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, the implied form being: "and when they were patient, We made from among them leaders" (ولما صبروا جعلنا منهم أئمة). كانوا: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the wāw of the plural being its noun; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿صبروا﴾; بآياتنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يوقنون; يوقنون: the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون﴾: إنّ: an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ربك is its noun; هو: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and the clause يفصل: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; or ﴿هو﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause ﴿يفصل﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause ﴿هو يفصل﴾ the khabar of إنّ; بينهم: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) يفصل; يوم: an adverb attached to يفصل; القيامة: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); فيما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفصل; كانوا: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the wāw of the plural being its noun; فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يختلفون; the clause ﴿يختلفون﴾ is the khabar of كان, and the clause ﴿كانوا فيه يختلفون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the wāw is a conjunction joining to something implied, the implied form being: "Have they been heedless, and has it not guided them?" (أغفلوا ولم يهد لهم), i.e. "has it not become clear (to them)?" (يتبيَّنْ). لم: a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; يهد: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is omitted, indicated by the context, the implied form being: "Has it not guided them, how many generations We destroyed?" (أولم يهد لهم كثرة إهلاكنا القرون). كم: the predicative kam (khabariyya), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أهلكنا; من قبلهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القرون; من القرون: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كم﴾; the clause ﴿يمشون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in لهم; في مساكنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يمشون.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات﴾: إن: a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: the postponed noun of إن.
﴿أفلا يسمعون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Have they gone deaf, so that they do not hear?" (أصموا فلا يسمعون). لا: negative; يسمعون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the wāw likewise is a conjunction joining to something implied; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; يروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); أنا: أنّ is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿نسوق﴾ is its khabar (predicate); الماء: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نسوق﴾; إلى الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نسوق﴾; الجرز: a naʿt (adjective) of الأرض; أنّ and what lies in its scope stand in place of the object of يروا.
﴿فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; نخرج: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "we"; the clause ﴿نخرج﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿نسوق﴾; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نخرج; زرعا: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿تأكل﴾ is an adjective of ﴿زرعا﴾; منه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تأكل; أنعامهم: the fāʿil of تأكل; أنفسهم: conjoined to أنعامهم.
﴿أفلا يبصرون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Have they gone blind, so that they do not see?" (أعموا فلا يبصرون). لا: negative; يبصرون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; يقولون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); متى: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); هذا: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); الفتح: a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; the clause ﴿ويقولون متى هذا الفتح﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إن: conditional; كنتم: كان, a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters), the tāʾ being its noun; صادقين: the khabar of كان; the clause ﴿كنتم صادقين﴾ is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون﴾: قل: an imperative verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); يوم: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لا ينفع﴾; الفتح: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); لا: negative; ينفع: an imperfect verb; الذين: the object of ينفع; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. إيمانهم: the postponed fāʿil of ﴿ينفع﴾; the wāw is a conjunction; لا: negative; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); ينظرون: an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿ينظرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (faṣīḥa); أعرض: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; عنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعرض; the wāw is a conjunction; انتظر: an imperative verb and a latent fāʿil, implied as "you", its object omitted. إنهم: إنّ is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿منتظرون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ [Translator's note: منتظرون is a single word (a noun), not a clause; translated as written]; منتظرون: an active participle, its object omitted.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
﴿الم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾: there is consensus on the nominative of تنزيل, and its nominative is from three angles:
First, as mubtadaʾ (subject), with ﴿لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ as the khabar (predicate); second, by an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this which is recited is a revelation (tanzīl)"; and third, in the sense of "these letters are a revelation", «ألم» indicating all the letters just as أ ب ت ث indicate them. If تنزيل were accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) it would be permissible, just as the Kufans read ﴿إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 3–5].

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾: «أم» indicates moving from one topic to another. ﴿بَلْ هُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); and likewise ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾. ﴿ما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾: i.e. the disbelievers have no protector who would prevent their punishment; ﴿وَلا شَفِيعٍ﴾: the nominative is also permissible, by [conjunction to] the position. ﴿أَفَلا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ this admonition.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read ﴿خَلْقَهُ﴾ with sukūn on the lām. Its accusative in this reading is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to Sībawayh, like ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]; according to others it is a badal (substitute) for «كلّ», i.e. "who perfected the creation of everything". On the school of some grammarians they are two objects, in the sense of "He made everything understand its creation". [The reading] ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾ takes it as a past verb in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of شيء. The meaning, according to what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, is: He made firm everything He created, i.e. He brought it as He willed and it did not deviate from His will. Another view is that everything He creates is good, because no one is able to produce its like, and it points to its Creator. Abū Isḥāq said: الذي أحسن كلَّ شيءٍ خلقُه is also permissible with the nominative, in the sense "that is His creation". ﴿وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنْسانِ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾: meaning Adam ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ﴾: derived from سللت الشيء ("I drew the thing out"), and the pattern فُعالة is for a small quantity. ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ مَهِينٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. weak; and someone else said: i.e. of no worth among people.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ﴾: meaning the water. ﴿وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِهِ﴾: i.e. that by which he lives. ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ﴾: He made السمع singular and الأبصار plural, because السمع is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a singular indicating a plural. ﴿وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾: plural of فؤاد, which is the heart.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وقالوا أأذا ضللنا في الأرض أأنا لفي خلق جديد﴾, and it is also read ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾. In this there is a difficult question of Arabic grammar. It is asked: what governs «إذ» [Translator's note: so in the text; إذا is meant], when what follows «إنّ» does not govern what precedes it? And the question is harder with the interrogative, because what follows an interrogative is even more fitting not to govern what precedes it than [what follows] «أنّ»; so how [can it], when the two have come together? The answer, according to the reading of whoever read أنا [Translator's note: i.e. إِنَّا without the interrogative], is that the governor is ضللنا; and according to the reading of whoever read ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾, that the governor is implied (muḍmar), the implied meaning being "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" There is also a question in it: it is asked, where is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا in the first reading, since it carries the sense of a condition? The answer to that is that it is followed by a past verb, and for that reason this is permissible. From Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa, that they read ﴿أَإِذا ضَلِلْنا﴾ [Translator's note: the distinctive vowelling (ضَلِلْنا, with kasra on the first lām) is not shown in the printed text], and it is an anomalous (shādhdh) dialect. And from al-Ḥasan: اإذا صللنا with ṣād; al-Farrāʾ related it thus, and claimed that it is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. صللنا is not known in the language, but صللنا is known [Translator's note: the vowel distinction between the two forms has been lost in the printed text; presumably صَلِلْنا is the unknown form and صَلَلْنا the known one]; one says صلّ اللحم وأصلّ, and خمّ وأخمّ, when [the meat] has gone rotten.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: it is from paying a number in full (tawfiyat al-ʿadad), i.e. he takes your number in full, all of you.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ناكِسُوا رُؤُسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq said: the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community, and the meaning is "If only you (plural) could see". The school of Abū al-ʿAbbās is otherwise: that the meaning is "O Muḥammad, say to the criminal: If you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, you would regret what you did"; the apodosis of «لو» and [the verb of] saying are omitted.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُداها﴾: two objects. It is said that there are two views on its meaning: one of them is that the context of the passage indicates that it concerns the Hereafter, i.e. if We willed, We would return them to the world and to the trial, as they asked. ﴿وَلكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾: i.e. the word from Me is due: I will surely punish whoever disobeys Me with the punishment of Hell; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knew that if He returned them they would go back, as He said: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعادُوا لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 28]. [Translator's note: the second view is not stated in the text.]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فَذُوقُوا بِما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا﴾: there are two views on its meaning: one is that it is from the forgetting that has no remembrance with it, i.e. you did not work for this day, so you were like those who forget; the other is that نسيتم means "you abandoned"; and likewise ﴿إِنَّا نَسِيناكُمْ﴾. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd adduced as proof His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنا إِلى آدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 115]. He said: the proof that it means "abandoned" is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, related of Iblīs that he said to him: ﴿ما نَهاكُما رَبُّكُما عَنْ هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 20]; so if Adam ﷺ had been forgetting, he [Iblīs] would have reminded him. And he recited [in the basīṭ metre]: 340-
كأنّه خارجا من جنب صفحته ... سفّود شرب نسوه عند مفتأد
(As though, jutting out from the side of its flank, it were the roasting-spit of a drinking party that they left behind at the fireplace.)
i.e. they left it; if it were from forgetting, they would have used it once.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّما يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنَا الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِّرُوا بِها خَرُّوا سُجَّداً﴾: i.e. only those believe in the signs, proofs and arguments who, when reminded of them, humble themselves before Allah and glorify Him with His praise. ﴿وَهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ from His worship nor from submitting to what He has made clear.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿تَتَجافى جُنُوبُهُمْ﴾: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or nominative because it is an imperfect verb; the inflection does not appear in it because it is a maqṣūr verb. The meaning of maqṣūr is that the inflection is withheld (quṣira) from it, and the meaning of manqūṣ is that the inflection is diminished (nuqiṣa) from it. ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿خَوْفاً﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿وَطَمَعاً﴾ is like it, i.e. out of fear of punishment and hope of reward. ﴿وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: «ما» may be in the sense of الذي ("that which") or a maṣdar; in both cases it must be written separately from «من».

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ﴾: it is also read ما أخفي لهم with sukūn on the yāʾ [i.e. أُخْفِيْ, "what I conceal"], as an imperfect verb. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ما نخفي ("what We conceal"), with nūn. Abū Isḥāq said: and it is read ما أخفي لهم [i.e. أَخْفى] in the sense of "what Allah has concealed for them". If you make «ما» in the sense of الذي ("that which"), it is in the position of the accusative on all the readings; and if you make it in the sense of أيّ ("which?") and read with the reading of the Medinans, it is in the position of the nominative, and if you read with another reading, it is in the position of the accusative.
﴿جَزاءً﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: [Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً لا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾.] Because the word «من» conveys a group, for this reason He said: لا يستوون ("they are not equal", plural). This is the view of many of the grammarians. Some of them said: يستوون is for two, except that two is a plural, because it is one gathered with another. The ḥadīth points to this view, because it is [reported] from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, and others, who said: ﴿أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً﴾ was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and ﴿كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً﴾ about al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: ﴿أَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described him with faith. The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿فَلَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ الْمَأْوى﴾, and the meaning is: "for him and those like him"; on this basis the plural came. And likewise ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا فَمَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ﴾. ﴿كُلَّما﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ﴾: a lām of oath. ﴿مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْأَدْنى﴾: i.e. the nearer; most of the exegetes hold that it is the calamities in this world.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾: i.e. to himself. ﴿مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِ﴾: i.e. with His proofs and signs. ﴿ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْها﴾ by refusing to accept; so know that He will take retribution on him. So He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ﴾: two objects. ﴿فَلا تَكُنْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقائِهِ﴾: we have already mentioned it. It has been said that its meaning is: "So be not in doubt about Moses ﷺ receiving the Book with acceptance." From al-Ḥasan, that he said regarding its meaning: "We certainly gave Moses the Book, and he was harmed and called a liar; so be not in doubt that what he met of denial and harm will meet you." This is an unusual view, besides being from the transmission of ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾: the Kufans read أمّة [Translator's note: so in the printed text; from what follows the Kufan reading meant is أَأِمَّة, with two realised hamzas], and it is a solecism (laḥn) according to all the grammarians, because it combines two hamzas in a single word. This is one of the subtleties of grammar, and its explanation is that the original is أَأْمِمَة; then the vowel of the first mīm was cast onto the hamza, the mīm was assimilated into the mīm, and the second hamza was lightened so that two hamzas would not come together. Combining two hamzas in two words is far-fetched; as for in one word, it is not permissible at all, except with lightening, [as in] آدم and آخر; and this is of the same kind as آدم. ﴿لَمَّا صَبَرُوا﴾ [read as لِما صبروا means] "because of their patience"; and ﴿لَمَّا صَبَرُوا﴾ means: when they were patient, We made them leaders.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ﴾: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Qatāda read أو لمن نهد لهم [Translator's note: so in the printed text; أَوَلَمْ نَهْدِ لَهُمْ is meant] with nūn, and this is a clear reading. The first reading, with yāʾ, has a difficulty in it, because it is said: a verb is never without an agent, so where is the agent of يهد? The grammarians discussed this. Al-Farrāʾ said: «كم» is in the position of the nominative by يهد.
This contradicts the principles of the grammarians in their saying that an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it, nor is كم in any way, I mean by what precedes it. The school of Abū al-ʿAbbās is that يهد indicates guidance, so the meaning is "Has the guidance not guided them?" It has also been said that the meaning is "Has Allah not guided them?", so that the meaning of the yāʾ and the meaning of the nūn are the same. Abū Isḥāq said: كم is in the position of the accusative by أهلكنا. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ﴾: in the position of the accusative by إنّ. ﴿أَفَلا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ in the sense of "Will they not accept?", like سمع الله لمن حمده ("Allah hears (accepts) the one who praises Him").

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَسُوقُ الْماءَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ﴾: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it is the land of Yemen. Sufyān said: and Maʿmar related to me from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: it is Abyan. Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān said from ʿIkrima: «إلى الأرض الجرز»: he said:
it is the thirsty [land]. Juwaybir said from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ﴾: he said: the dead, parched [land]. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the one in which there is no vegetation. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: الأرض الجرز is the one that grows nothing. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is unlikely to be anything but a specific land, because of the entry of the alif and lām, except that it is permissible on the view of what Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said. Abū Jaʿfar said: the chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās is sound, with no flaw in it; and this is only a naʿt (adjective), and the adjective of a definite noun is with the alif and lām. It is derived from their saying رجل جروز ("a voracious man"), when he leaves nothing without eating it. Al-Farrāʾ and others related that one says أرض جُرُز, جُرْز and جَرَز [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant forms is not given in the printed text; supplied here from the standard lexical sources], and likewise بخل, رعب and رهب: in the four there are four dialects. ﴿فَنُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً﴾: it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نسوق, or cut off from what precedes it. ﴿تَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ أَنْعامُهُمْ﴾: in the position of the accusative as a naʿt. ﴿وَأَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾: i.e. and they eat of it. In the speech of the Arabs النفس is of two kinds: one is that separateness is meant by it, and the other is that the whole of a thing and its reality is meant by it. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116], i.e. You know what I know and I do not know what You know. ﴿أَفَلا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾: (ألا) may be for drawing attention (tanbīh).

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْفَتْحُ﴾: «متى» is in the position of the nominative, and it may be in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). Al-Farrāʾ said: He means the conquest of Mecca. Better than this is what Mujāhid said; he said:
He means the Day of Resurrection. Abū Jaʿfar said: on the day of the conquest of Mecca, the faith of whoever believed did benefit him. It is related that the believers said: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will judge between us on the Day of Resurrection, and will reward the doer of good and punish the evildoer," so the disbelievers said mockingly: "When is this fatḥ?", i.e. this judgement. A judge is called فاتح and فتّاح because matters are opened up and decided at his hands; and in the Quran: ﴿رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ﴾: [accusative] as an adverb (ẓarf); al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾: it is said that its meaning is: turn away from their foolishness and do not answer them except with what you have been commanded.
﴿وَانْتَظِرْ إِنَّهُمْ مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾: i.e. wait for the Day of the fatḥ, the day on which Allah will judge in your favour against them. If someone says: how can they be waiting for the Day of Resurrection when they do not believe in it? — there are two answers to this: one is that the meaning is that they are waiting for death, which is one of the causes of the Resurrection, so this would be figurative; and the other is that among them are some who doubt and some who are certain of the Resurrection, so this would be for these two kinds. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقاً﴾? [Verse 18].
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It was revealed concerning two men of Quraysh, up to the end of the three verses.
Ibn Abī Laylā said: It was revealed concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's blessings be upon him, and a man of Quraysh.
And it is said: It was revealed concerning "ʿAlī", peace be upon him, and "al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ".
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, bore witness for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to faith, and that he is in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ فَلَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾.
It came in the plural because two constitute a group; and it applies to all the believers, even though the occasion of revelation was specific, because of the indefiniteness (ibhām) of "مَنْ".

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَكْبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
Abū al-Ḍuḥā narrated from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾ — he said: the Day of Badr.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: so that whoever of them remains may repent.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾ — he said: years [of drought] that struck a people before you.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾ — he said: the ḥudūd (prescribed penalties).
ʿAlqama, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the calamities in this world.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: killing, and hunger for Quraysh in this world.
﴿دُونَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَكْبَرِ﴾: the Day of Resurrection, in the Hereafter.
Abū Yaḥyā narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿الْعَذَابُ الأَدْنَى﴾ is the punishment of the grave and the punishment of this world.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Mujāhid, who said: the calamities.
These statements are not contradictory; they come back to the meaning of ﴿ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾ being whatever is before the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ فَلاَ تَكُن فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِ﴾.
It is said: the hāʾ (the pronoun "him/it") refers to the Book, and the name of Moses ﷺ is implied (muḍmar).
And the meaning «[Translator's note: i.e. on the other view]»: the hāʾ refers to Moses, and the Book has been omitted because it was mentioned before; and this is preferable.
The meaning is: so do not be in doubt about Moses' receiving the Book with acceptance; and addressing the Prophet ﷺ is addressing all people.
It is possible that the meaning is: say to this doubter.
It is possible that the meaning is: so do not be in doubt about receiving this report with acceptance.
Qatāda said: Its meaning is: so do not be in doubt that you met him — or will meet him — on the night he was taken on the Night Journey.
Some of the people of knowledge chose this view, because Ibn ʿAbbās narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey I was shown Moses son of ʿImrān, a tall, brown-complexioned man with curly hair, as though he were one of the men of Shanūʾa…" — the ḥadīth.
So the implied sense on this view of ﴿فَلاَ تَكُن فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِ﴾ is that he did see Moses on the night he was taken on the Night Journey.
And he interpreted ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُ﴾ as meaning "and We made Moses" ﴿هُدًى﴾, that is, right guidance, ﴿لِّبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾: they are rightly guided by following him and attain the truth by taking him as an example.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِّبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — he said: Allah made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ﴾.
That is: have We not made clear to them?

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلْمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْجُرُزِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is the land that does not produce vegetation.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the land in which there is no vegetation.
Abū Jaʿfar said: الجُزُرُ in the language means dry land, needing water, in which there is no vegetation, as though it has eaten up what was in it; and from it is said: رجلٌ جَرُوزٌ (a "jarūz" man), when he is a great eater. «[Translator's note: the text as printed has الجُزُرُ (with zāy then rāʾ) here, whereas the Qurʾānic word under discussion is ٱلْجُرُزِ; translated as written.]»

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَـٰذَا ٱلْفَتْحُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is the Day of Resurrection.
Qatāda said: الفَتْحُ is the judgment (al-qaḍāʾ).
Al-Farrāʾ and al-Qutabī said: the conquest of Mecca.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قُلْ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَتْحِ لاَ يَنفَعُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِيَمَانُهُمْ﴾.
It was called "fatḥ" because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, grants victory (yaftaḥu) to the believers in it.
Or because by the judgment in it — as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿رَبَّنْا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ﴾, that is, judge. «[Translator's note: the sentence "أو لأنَّ بالقضاء فيه" appears incomplete in the source; translated as written.]»

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَٱنتَظِرْ إِنَّهُمْ مُّنتَظِرُونَ﴾.
Then this was abrogated by the command to fight.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: this is the sending down of the Book.
It has also been said: the meaning is: ﴿الۤـمۤ﴾ is part of the sending down of the Book.
It is also possible that the meaning is: the sending down of the Book — there is no doubt in it.
We have explained the meaning of ﴿الۤـمۤ﴾ and ﴿لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَاهُ﴾.
That is, nay, do they say he has invented it?

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُدَبِّرُ ٱلأَمْرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, He issues the decree in heaven, then sends it down to the earth.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This verse is problematic, since He said in another place: ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾.
The people of exegesis have several views on it:
a- Among them is what Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾, he said: This is in this world. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made for the unbelievers the length of fifty thousand years.
b- And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us, saying: Abū Dāwūd Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us.
He said: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾, he said: [It is] what lies between the lowest part of the earth and the Throne.
c- Ibn Abī Najīḥ said from Mujāhid, and about that he said: This world, from its beginning to its end, is fifty thousand years; no one knows how much of it has passed nor how much remains.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has also been said: the Day of Resurrection consists of days; part of it is the length of a thousand years and part of it the length of fifty thousand years.
Abū Jaʿfar said: "Day" (yawm) in the language has the sense of "time" (waqt). So the meaning on this view is: the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him, at one time whose length is a thousand years, and at another time more than that — an ascent greater than that — whose length is fifty thousand years.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: He perfected it.
He said: It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ﴾.
That is, He did not create man in the form of a beast, nor create the beast in the form of man.
It has also been said: that is, it did not defeat Him.
The best that has been said about this is what Khuṣayf related from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾: he said: He did well in His creating; He made the dog good in its creation.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of this is: He did well in His action, as you say: so-and-so did well in cutting off [the hand of] the thief.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُ مِن سُلاَلَةٍ مِّن مَّآءٍ مَّهِينٍ﴾.
﴿السُّلاَلةُ﴾ is [used] for the small amount that slips out (yansallu), and (المَهِينُ) is the weak.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾.
It is related from al-Ḥasan that he read ﴿صَلَلْنَا﴾ (with ṣād) with fatḥa on the lām, and some related it with kasra on the lām.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ضَلَلْنَا﴾ means we have been destroyed.
