Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿ضَلَلْنَا﴾ is: we have become dust and bones and can no longer be distinguished; and this comes back to the view of Mujāhid.
The meaning of "صَلَلْنَا" with fatḥa on the lām is: we have become putrid and changed, and our forms have changed. It is said ṣalla al-laḥmu and aṣalla when meat becomes putrid and changes.
It may also be from al-ṣalla, which is dry ground. Ṣalilnā with kasra on the lām is not known.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذِ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ رَبَّنَآ أَبْصَرْنَا وَسَمِعْنَا فَٱرْجِعْنَا نَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً﴾.
There is an omission in the wording; the meaning is: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذِ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾, you would see something from which you would take a severe lesson.
And the meaning is: saying, "Our Lord"; so the verb of saying is omitted as well.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لآتَيْنَا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُدَاهَا﴾.
That is, had We willed, We would have shown them a sign compelling them to believe, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنْ حَقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, because of their sins.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
Qatāda related from Anas, who said: They stay awake between the evening (al-ʿishāʾ) and the dark of night (al-ʿatama), and pray.
ʿAṭāʾ said: They do not sleep before ʿIshāʾ until they have prayed it.
Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: They pray in the depth of the night.
Mālik and al-Awzāʿī said the same.
This view is the most likely of them, for two reasons:
One of them: Abū Wāʾil related from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: Shall I not direct you to the deeds of good? Fasting is a shield; charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire; and a man's prayer in the depth of the night. Then he recited ﴿تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ﴾ up to ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
The other reason is that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, known as al-Jarījī, narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, saying: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to read ﴿مِنْ قُرَّاتِ أَعْيُنٍ﴾. So this fits the night prayer better, because they were recompensed for what they concealed with what is concealed.
Abū Salama related from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Your Lord said: (I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of a human being.) Recite, if you wish: ﴿فَلاَ تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوْا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾."

safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(تنزيل) a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) [Note: or it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. the Qur'an.. and likewise the clause «لا ريب فيه» and the preposition and its genitive noun (من ربّ العالمين); so they are three independent clauses.], its khabar being (من ربّ), (لا) the lā of generic negation, (ريب) the noun of لا, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, (فيه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of لا, (من رب) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ تنزيل [Note: or it is a khabar after a khabar.. and it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (فيه)].
The clause «تنزيل الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «لا ريب فيه..» has no grammatical position: parenthetical [Note: or it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of الكتاب.].

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل together with the hamza, (بل) for iḍrāb (digression) of cancellation (ibṭālī) of their saying افتراه, (من ربّك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) الحقّ — or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it —, (اللام) of causation, (تنذر) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām.. and the second object is implied, its implied form being العقاب (the punishment).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تنذر) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أنزلناه.
(ما) negative, (نذير) genitive (majrūr) in its outward form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the fāʿil (agent) of أتاهم, (من قبلك) attached to (أتاهم) [Note: or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of نذير.].
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «افتراه ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «هو الحقّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تنذر قوما..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ما أتاهم من نذير..» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt of (قوما).
The clause «لعلّهم يهتدون..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يهتدون..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:4-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الذي) a relative noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الله, in the position of a nominative, (الواو) conjunction in the three places, (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to السموات, (بينهما) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, (في ستة) attached to (خلق), (ثمّ) a conjunction, (على العرش) attached to (استوى), (ما) negative, (لكم) attached to an omitted fronted khabar, (وليّ) genitive (majrūr) in its outward form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation, (الهمزة) for the interrogative, (الفاء) conjunction, (لا) negative..
The clause «الله الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «استوى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خلق.
The clause «ما لكم من دونه..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: the clause may be the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله), and the relative (الذي) is then a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty or a badal (substitute).].
The clause «تتذكّرون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: have you been heedless, so you do not remember ...
(5) (من السماء) attached to (يدبّر) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the meaning of ينقل (transfers), (إلى الأرض) attached to (يدبّر), (إليه) attached to (يعرج), and the fāʿil (agent) of يعرج is a pronoun referring to الأمر, (في يوم) attached to (يعرج), (ممّا) attached to a naʿt of ألف سنة.
The clause «يدبّر..» is in the position of a nominative as another khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يعرج..» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يدبّر.
The clause «كان مقداره ألف ...» is in the position of a genitive as a naʿt of يوم.
The clause «تعدّون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(6) (ذلك) a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is عالم, (العزيز) a second khabar, nominative, (الرحيم) a third khabar, nominative.
The clause «ذلك عالم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
(7) (الذي) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, a fourth khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك [Note: or it is a naʿt of الرحيم.], (من طين) attached to (بدأ).
The clause «أحسن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
The clause «بدأ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أحسن.
The clause «خلقه ...» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt of كلّ.. or in the position of a genitive as a naʿt of شيء.
(8) (من سلالة) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعل, (من ماء) attached to a naʿt of سلالة.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause بدأ.
(9) (فيه) attached to (نفخ), (من روحه) attached to (نفخ), and the annexation of the spirit to Him the Exalted is for honouring, (لكم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being جعل, (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), its governor being تشكرون, (ما) redundant, to emphasise the paucity.
The clause «سوّاه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause جعل.
The clause «نفخ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause جعل.
The clause «جعل لكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first clause جعل.
The clause «تشكرون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مهين): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral مهن, of the pattern كرم (category karuma), i.e. to be base and weak; its pattern is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, the Exalted, «فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ», i.e. in a prolonged stretch of time; the actual number is not what is meant. The prolonged duration was expressed by "the thousand" because it is the furthest of the ranks and the utmost of limits, and there is no rank above it, except the numbers of its ranks that branch out from it.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī) in both places, (في الأرض) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ضللنا), (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun, (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), (في خلق) attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, (بل) for iḍrāb (digression) of transition (intiqālī), (بلقاء) attached to the khabar (كافرون).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ضللنا ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّا لفي خلق جديد..» has no grammatical position: an explication of the implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e.: we will be resurrected, or we will be brought out [Note: it was not permitted to attach (إذا) to جديد — i.e. it was not valid for the clause إنّا لفي.. to be the apodosis — because what comes after إنّ does not govern what precedes it.].
The clause «هم ... كافرون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (وكل) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, and it is the linking pronoun, (بكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وكّل), (إلى ربّكم) attached to (ترجعون), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتوفّاكم ملك ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «وكّل بكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ترجعون ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the speech reported.
(12) (الواو) conjunction, (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle, and the object of (ترى), which is of sight, is omitted, indicated by the mubtadaʾ (subject) after it, i.e.: المجرمون, (إذ) an adverb borrowed for future time, attached to (ترى) [Note: this is the explanation of Abū al-Baqāʾ.. or the adverb of the past (إذ) was used because the occurrence of the seeing is certain.], (عند) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (ناكسو), (ربّنا) the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative, (الفاء) conjunction, to link the effect to the cause, (نعمل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the request, (صالحا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun).], (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun..
The clause «لو ترى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل..
The apodosis of لو is omitted, i.e.: you would have seen an amazing matter.
The clause «المجرمون ناكسو..» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The vocative clause and its response: in the position of an accusative as the speech reported of an implied verb of saying, which is in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: «يقولون ربّنا ...».
The clause «أبصرنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «سمعنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «ارجعنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «نعمل ...» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e.: if You return us, we will do [righteousness]; so the clause has no grammatical position.
The clause «إنّا موقنون..» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(13) (الواو) conjunction, (اللام) linking the apodosis of لو, (هداها) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, (الواو) conjunction, (لكن) for istidrāk (rectification), (منّي) attached to a ḥāl of القول, (اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath, (أملأن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative, (من الجنّة) attached to (أملأن), (أجمعين) a ḥāl, accusative, of الجنّة and الناس ...
The clause «لو شئنا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لو ترى ...
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «حقّ القول ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause شئنا.
The clause «أملأنّ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath [Note: the oath may be His saying: حقّ القول منّي, i.e. I swear I will surely fill.].
(14) (الفاء) conjunction, (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle, and the object of ذوقوا is omitted, i.e.:
taste the punishment [Note: the object may be the demonstrative (هذا), i.e. this punishment.], (هذا) a demonstrative in the position of a badal (substitute) of يومكم.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما نسيتم..) is in the position of a genitive by (الباء) — which is of causation — attached to (ذوقوا).
(ما كنتم) is like ما نسيتم.. and the interpreted maṣdar is like the first, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the second (ذوقوا).
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is conjoined to an implied speech reported of an implied verb of saying, i.e.: it was said to them: you abandoned faith, so taste....
The clause «إنّا نسيناكم ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «نسيناكم....» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «ذوقوا (the second)» is conjoined to the clause ذوقوا (the first).
The two clauses «نسيتم، كنتم ...» have no grammatical position: the ṣilas of the two particle-relatives (ما).
The clause «تعملون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(12) ناكسو: plural of ناكس, an active participle from the triliteral نكس; its pattern is فاعل.
(14) الخلد: maṣdar of the triliteral خلد, of the pattern نصر (category naṣara); it is the noun from it meaning permanence and continuance; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Shifting from the verbal to the nominal: in His saying, the Exalted, «ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رؤسهم ... up to His saying, the Exalted, إنا موقنون».
It is a shift from the verbal clause to the emphasised nominal clause, to show their firmness in certainty and the completeness of their desire for it; all of that is for earnestness in the plea, out of hope of being answered in what they asked of the return — and how could that be theirs!

* Benefits:
(1) - The bare (mujarrad) and augmented (mazīd) verbs:
1- The bare verb: it is that all of whose letters are radical, none of which can be dispensed with; it is triliteral, such as: كتب - عدّ, and quadriliteral, such as: دحرج - عسكر.
2- The augmented: it is the verb to whose radical letters an addition of one, two or three letters has occurred:
a- The augmented triliteral: the triliteral is augmented by one, two or three letters:
1- Augmented by one letter, and it has three patterns:
a- أفعل: such as: أكرم - أحسن - أعلم..
b- فعّل: قدّم - نظّم - سوّى.
c- فاعل: شارك - نازل - سامح.
2- Augmented by two letters, and it has six patterns:
a- افتعل: اجتمع - انتصر - افتتح.
b- انفعل: انكسر - انقلب - اندفع.
c- تفاعل: تشارك - تمارض - تلاعب.
d- تفعّل: تقدّم - تنظّم - تعوّد.
e- افعلّ: احمرّ - اخضرّ.
and افعالّ: اصفارّ - احمارّ.
3- Augmented by three letters, and it has two patterns: a- استفعل: استخرج - استعمل - استخدم.
b- افعوعل: اخشوشن - اعشوشب - اخضوضر.
b- The augmented quadriliteral.
1- The quadriliteral is augmented by one letter, and it has one pattern:
تفعلل: تدحرج - تبعثر. 2- And it is augmented by two letters, and it has two patterns:
a- افعللّ: اقشعرّ - اطمأنّ - ادلهمّ.
b- افعنلل: احرنجم (meaning "gathered") افرنقع.
Remark:
1- The letters of augmentation are gathered in the word (سألتمونيها). 2- When judging a verb to be augmented or bare, we return it to the past tense and then judge it.
3- The prefixes of the imperfect, the attached pronouns, the nūn of emphasis or the tāʾ of the feminine that join the verb have no relation to augmentation or reduction; they are left out of the reckoning.
4- Augmentation is not only by adding a letter; it is also by doubling a letter: (فهم) becomes (فهّم), and this augmentation is called «doubling» (taḍʿīf). Or we say: the verb is augmented by doubling.
(2) - Emphasis with أجمعين:
(أجمعون) is distinguished among the words of semantic emphasis (tawkīd maʿnawī), and differs from its sisters, in that it does not need a pronoun attached to it referring back to the emphasised word, as has come in the verse we are dealing with, namely His saying, the Exalted, وَلكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ. But if «أجمعون» is preceded by an emphasis, it is regarded as an emphasis strengthening the first emphasis, as in His saying, the Exalted, فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ. As for كله, it is followed by أجمع, such as: (جاء الفريق كله أجمع). And كلها by جمعاء, such as (اشتركت العشير كلّها جمعاء), and كلهن by جمع, such as: عملت النسوة كلهن جمع. As for «جميعا», it comes as a ḥāl and is not parsed as tawkīd (emphasis).

safi-cedvel:15-18.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restraining particle (kāffa) and a restrained one (makfūfa), (بآياتنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمن), (بها) attached to (ذكّروا), (بحمد) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of سبّحوا, (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya), (لا) negative.
The clause «إنّما يؤمن بآياتنا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «خرّوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «سبّحوا....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «هم لا يستكبرون..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يستكبرون..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(16) (عن المضاجع) attached to (تتجافى), (خوفا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) [Note: or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl.. or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; and likewise طمعا.], (مما) attached to (ينفقون), and the linking pronoun is omitted.
The clause «تتجافى جنوبهم..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of سبّحوا [Note: it may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «يدعون..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in جنوبهم [Note: it may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «ينفقون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يستكبرون [Note: or conjoined to the clause يدعون, taking its i'rab.].
(17) (الفاء) conjunction, (لا) negative, (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: or an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is the khabar, and the interrogative clause is the object of تعلم, since the verb is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.], and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (أخفي) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring to ما, (لهم) attached to (أخفي), (من قرّة) attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun of the nāʾib fāʿil, (جزاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi, accusative, its governor being أخفي [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e.: they were recompensed with a recompense.], (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun, in the position of a genitive, the governor being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ — which is of causation — attached to جزاء.
The clause «لا تعلم نفس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّما يؤمن ...
The clause «أخفي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «كانوا يعملون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative or the nominal relative (ما).
The clause «يعملون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(18) (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), (الفاء) conjunction, (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, (كمن) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, (لا) negative.
The clause «من كان مؤمنا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative (من).
The clause «كان فاسقا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «لا يستوون..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(تتجافى): it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is تتجافي with a yāʾ at its end; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif; and the alif's origin is a wāw in the triliteral.

* Benefits:
- The single kāf:
It is the one that makes genitive, and it divides into a particle and a noun. As for the particle, it has five meanings:
1- Likening (tashbīh), as in «زيد كالأسد» and His saying, the Exalted, أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً.
2- Causation (taʿlīl): some affirmed it and most denied it; its example is His saying, the Exalted, وَيْكَأَنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الْكافِرُونَ, i.e. I wonder at their not prospering, and His saying, the Exalted, كَما أَرْسَلْنا فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا; al-Akhfash said: on account of My sending among you a messenger.
3- Being over (istiʿlāʾ): al-Akhfash and the Kufans mentioned it, and [reported] that one of them was asked: How are you this morning? and he said: كخير, i.e. on good. It was said the meaning is: بخير (well), and it was said: it is for likening with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. like one possessing good.
4- Promptness (mubādara): that is when it is joined to (ما), as in (سلم كما تدخل) (give greeting as soon as you enter) and (وصلّ كما يدخل الوقت) (pray as soon as the time comes in).
5- Emphasis (tawkīd): it is the redundant one (zāʾida), as in His saying, the Exalted, لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ.
As for the nominal kāf that makes genitive, it is synonymous with مثل (like), and it occurs only in poetic necessity, as in the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
بيض ثلاث كنعاج جمّ ... يضحكن عن كالبرد المنهمّ
(Three fair ones, like hornless ewes, who smile showing [teeth] like melting hail.)
المنهمّ: melting; and the evidence is his saying: كالبرد, i.e. like hail. Many, among them al-Akhfash and al-Fārisī, said: it is permitted in free choice (ikhtiyār), so they permitted in such as «زيد كالأسد» that the kāf be in the position of a nominative as a khabar meaning مثل, with الأسد as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

safi-cedvel:19-21.t:
* I'rab:
(أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing, (الواو) conjunction, and (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (لهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) جنّات, (نزلا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of جنّات, (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by (الباء) — which is of causation — attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) which is the khabar.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause آمنوا..
The clause «لهم جنّات ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «يعملون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(20) (الواو) conjunction, (أمّا ... النار) like أما ... جنّات, (كلّما) an adverb containing the sense of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis أعيدوا, (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, (منها) attached to (يخرجوا), and (الواو) in (أعيدوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), (فيها) attached to (أعيدوا), (لهم) attached to (قيل), (الذي) a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب), (به) attached to (تكذّبون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجوا..) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being أرادوا.
The clause «الذين فسقوا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «فسقوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «مأواهم النار..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «الذين».
The clause «أرادوا....» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يخرجوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أعيدوا فيها..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قيل لهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of a nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil [Note: originally it is the clause of the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).].
The clause «كنتم به تكذّبون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تكذّبون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كنتم.
(21) (الواو) conjunction, (اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath, (نذيقنّهم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative.. and (النون) is for emphasis, and (هم) is the mafʿūl bihi, (من العذاب) attached to (نذيقنّهم), (دون) an adverb, accusative, attached to (نذيقنّهم).
The clause «نذيقنّهم..» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath. And the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لعلّهم يرجعون..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرجعون..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (من) an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of a nominative, its khabar (predicate) being (أظلم), (ممّن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم, (بآيات) attached to (ذكّر), (عنها) attached to (أعرض), (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun, (من المجرمين) attached to (منتقمون).
The clause «من أظلم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ذكّر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «أعرض عنها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «إنّا ... منتقمون.» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(منتقمون): plural of منتقم, an active participle from the five-letter verb انتقم; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The conjunctions have secrets, so it is not valid to put some of them in the place of others, because of the differences between them; and the word ثم in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْها» is for expressing unlikelihood (istibʿād).
The meaning: turning away from the like of Allah's signs — in their clarity, their illumination and their guidance to the right path and to winning the supreme happiness — after being reminded of them is something unlikely in reason and in justice; just as you say to your companion: you found such an opportunity, then (ثم) you did not seize it — expressing how unlikely it was that he would leave off seizing it.

safi-cedvel:23-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath, (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition, (لا) prohibitive, making jussive, (في مرية) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of تكن, (من لقائه) attached to مرية [Note: on the referent of the pronoun the exegetes have many views.], and the third-person pronoun in (جعلناه) refers to Moses — or to the Book —, (هدى) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعلناه, (لبني) attached to هدى.
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تكن في مرية ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you ask about it, then do not be.. [Note: and the clause of the condition and its apodosis has no grammatical position: parenthetical.].
The clause «جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
(24) (الواو) conjunction in both places, (منهم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being جعلنا, (بأمرنا) attached to (يهدون), (لمّا) an indeclinable (mabnī) adverb containing the sense of condition — or stripped of the condition — attached to the content of the apodosis — or to (جعلنا) —, (بآياتنا) attached to (يوقنون).
The clause «جعلنا....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «يهدون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of أئمة.
The clause «صبروا....» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «كانوا ... يوقنون..» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause صبروا..
The clause «يوقنون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(25) (هو) a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the clause يفصل, (بينهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يفصل), (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يفصل), (في ما) attached to (يفصل), (فيه) attached to (يختلفون).
The clause «إنّ ربّك ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هو يفصل ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يفصل ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of (هو).
The clause «كانوا.. يختلفون.» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يختلفون..» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:26-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), (الواو) conjunction, (لهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يهد) in the sense of "become clear", and the pronoun in it refers to the people of Mecca, and the fāʿil (agent) of يهد is omitted, indicated by the context of speech in His saying أهلكناه, i.e.: has not Our destroying become clear to them.. (من قبلهم) attached to (أهلكنا) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of القرون.], (من القرون) the tamyīz (specification) of كم, (في مساكنهم) attached to (يمشون), (في ذلك) attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, (اللام) for emphasis, (الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke (taqrīʿī), (الفاء) conjunction, (لا) negative.
The clause «لم يهد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
were they heedless, and has it not become clear ...
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or an explication of the fāʿil —. The clause «يمشون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of القرون [Note: or of the pronoun in (لهم).. and it may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسمعون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
has deafness struck them, so that they do not hear.
(أولم يروا) is like أولم يهد.. (أنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun, (إلى الأرض) attached to (نسوق), (به) attached to (نخرج), and (الباء) is of causation, (منه) attached to (تأكل), (أفلا يبصرون) like أفلا يسمعون.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا نسوق ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يروا..
The clause «لم يروا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم يهد.
The clause «نسوق ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «نخرج ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause نسوق.
The clause «تأكل منه أنعامهم..» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (زرعا).
The clause «يبصرون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
has blindness struck them, so that they do not see.

* Morphology:
(الجرز): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from جرزت تجرز الأرض — of the pattern فرح (category fariḥa) — meaning that it does not grow [vegetation], or its vegetation has been eaten; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas; its plural is أجراز.

* Rhetoric:
The art of correspondence (al-munāsaba): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ» — the verse.
Correspondence is of two kinds: either correspondence in meanings, or correspondence in wordings; what concerns us in this verse is the first kind, and its definition is: that the speaker begins with a meaning, then completes his speech with what corresponds to it in meaning, not in wording.
For He, the Exalted, said at the head of the verse: أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ, and it is an admonition by hearing, since they had not looked upon the destroyed generations but had only heard of them; so it was fitting that He bring after it His saying «أَفَلا يَسْمَعُونَ». As for after the visible admonition, which is His saying after this verse «أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَسُوقُ الْماءَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ», it was fitting that He say «أَفَلا يُبْصِرُونَ», because crops are seen, not heard — so that the end of each speech corresponds to its beginning.

* Benefits:
- Removing a misconception:
Among the misconceptions about this verse is the saying of Ibn ʿUṣfūr, regarding His saying, the Exalted, in this verse أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا, that (كم) is the fāʿil of يهد. If you say: he derived it according to a dialect that al-Akhfash reported, namely that some Arabs do not insist on the predicative (khabariyya) (كم) coming first, I say: he admitted its poor quality, so deriving the Revelation upon it after that is poor. The correct view is that the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, i.e. has not Allah made clear to them, or to guidance; the first is the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ and the second the saying of al-Zajjāj. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the fāʿil is the clause — and it has preceded that the fāʿil cannot be a clause — and «كم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أهلكنا, and the clause is the object of يهد, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from it; «and the predicative كم causes suspension, contrary to most of them». Imam al-Nasafī mentioned that the fāʿil is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as evidenced by the reading of Zayd from Yaʿqūb (أولم تهد لهم).

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (متى) an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هذا, (الفتح) a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) —, (كنتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «متى هذا الفتح ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كنتم صادقين..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لا ينفع), (لا) negative, (الذين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is (إيمانهم), (الواو) conjunction, (لا) like the first, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in (ينظرون) is the wāw.
The clause «قل....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا ينفع ... إيمانهم.» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا هم ينظرون ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause لا ينفع.
The clause «ينظرون..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(30) (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition, (عنهم) attached to (أعرض), (الواو) conjunction.
The clause «أعرض عنهم ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.:
if they turn away from you, then turn away.
The clause «انتظر....» is conjoined to the clause أعرض....
The clause «إنّهم منتظرون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious.
His saying: {تَنزِيلُ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is the khabar of «ألم», because «ألم» is meant to denote the sūra and part of the Qur'an; and «تنزيلُ» is in the sense of «مُنزَّل» ("sent down"). The sentence {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is a ḥāl from «الكتاب», and the governing element in it is «تنزيلُ», because it is a maṣdar. And «مِنْ رَبِّ» is attached to it as well. It is also possible that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه» because it occurs as a khabar; the governing element in it is the adverbial phrase or the notion of "being settled".
The second: «تَنْزِل» [sic] is a mubtadaʾ and «لا ريبَ فيه» is its khabar, and {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه». It is then not permissible for it to be attached to «تنزيل», because the maṣdar has been predicated of and so does not govern; but one who is liberal about prepositions does not care about that. [Translator's note: the source reads «تَنْزِل» here, apparently for «تنزيلُ»; translated as written.]
The third: «تنزيلُ» is also a mubtadaʾ, «مِنْ رَبِّ» its khabar, and «لا ريبَ» a ḥāl or a parenthetical. The fourth: «لا ريب» and {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} are two khabars of «تنزيلُ». The fifth: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and likewise «لا ريبَ», and likewise «مِنْ ربّ», so that each sentence is independent by itself. It is also possible that they are two ḥāls from «تنزيلُ», and that «مِنْ رب» is the ḥāl and «لا ريبَ» parenthetical. The beginning of al-Baqara is a guide to this; I repeated it only to refresh it.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} to be attached to «تنزيل», saying: "by fronting and postponing." The Shaykh rejected it: if we say {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is parenthetical, there is no fronting and postponing; indeed, had it been postponed it would not be parenthetical. He also allowed that it be attached to «لا ريبَ», that is, "there is no doubt about it from the side of the Lord of the worlds"; and if doubt occurred among the disbelievers, that is not taken into account.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: it is the disconnected «أم», and the iḍrāb (turning away) is a transition, not a refutation.
His saying: {بَلْ هُوَ الحق}: a second iḍrāb. Had it been said that it is an iḍrāb of refutation of «افتراه» alone, it would have been correct; and on this it is said: every iḍrāb in the Qur'an is a transition except this one, for it may be a refutation, because it refutes their statement, that is, "it is not, as they said, a fabrication; rather it is the truth". In al-Zamakhsharī's discourse is something that guides to this, for he said: "The pronoun in «فيه» returns to the content of the sentence, as if it were said: there is no doubt about that, that is, about its being from the Lord of the worlds. In support of its soundness is His saying {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ: افتراه}, because their statement 'this is fabricated' is a denial that it is from the Lord of the worlds; and likewise His saying {بَلْ هُوَ الحق مِن رَّبِّكَ} contains the affirmation that it is from Allah. This is a sound, firm style."
His saying: «مِنْ ربِّك»: a ḥāl from «الحقّ»; its governing element is omitted by the rule, and it is also the governing element of «لِتُنْذِرَ». The governing element of «لتنذر» may also be another, that is, "He sent it down so that you may warn".
His saying: {قَوْماً مَّآ أَتَاهُم}: the apparent view is that the second object of the warning is omitted, and «قوماً» is the first, the implied form being "so that you may warn a people of the punishment"; and «ما أتاهم» is a negated sentence in the position of accusative as an adjective of «قوماً». He means: those in the interval between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad, peace be upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī made it like His saying {لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 6]. On this, «مِنْ نذير» is the fāʿil of «أتاهم», and «مِنْ» is redundant in it, and «مِنْ قبلِك» is an adjective of «نذير». It is also possible that «مِنْ قبلك» be attached to «أتاهم».
The Shaykh allowed «ما» to be relative in both places, and the implied form is: "so that you may warn a people of the punishment that came to them from a warner before you." «مِنْ نذير» is attached to «أتاهم», that is, "it came to them on the tongue of a warner before you"; likewise {لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 6], that is, "the punishment with which their fathers were warned". So «ما» is an object in both places, and «لِتُنْذرَ» governs two objects. The Exalted said: {فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً} [Fuṣṣilat: 13]. This view runs along the apparent sense of the Qur'an. The Exalted said: {وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ} [Fāṭir: 24] and {أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلاَ نَذِيرٍ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ} [al-Māʾida: 19]. I say: what he said is apparent.
It appears that in the other verse there is another analysis: that «ما» is a maṣdar particle, its implied form being "so that you may warn a people with a warning like the warning of their fathers", because all the messengers agree on the word of truth.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ}: the majority read it active. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it passive. The origin is «يُعْرَجُ به», then the preposition was omitted so the pronoun became nominative and latent. It is anomalous (shādhdh), and is suited to justify the like of it.
His saying: «مِمَّا تَعُدُّون»: the majority read it in the second person. Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī, Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it in the third person. This prepositional phrase is an adjective of «أَلْف» or of «سَنة».

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {ذلك عَالِمُ}: the majority read «عالمُ», «العزيز» and «الرحيم» in the nominative, with «ذلك» as a mubtadaʾ and «عالمُ» its khabar, and «العزيز الرحيم» two khabars or two adjectives; or «العزيز الرحيم» is a mubtadaʾ with its adjective and «الذي أَحْسَنَ» its khabar; or «العزيزُ الرحيم» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read all three in the genitive. Its analysis, with its difficulty, is that «ذلك» points to the managed affair (al-amr al-mudabbar) and is the fāʿil of «يَعْرُجُ», and the three attributes are a badal for the pronoun in «إليه», as if it were said: "then the managed affair ascends to Him, the Knower of the unseen", that is, to the Knower of the unseen.
Abū Zayd read «عالمُ» in the nominative and «العزيزِ الرحيمِ» in the genitive, so that «ذلك عالمُ» is mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «العزيزِ الرحيمِ» are two badals from the hāʾ in «إليه» as well, with the sentence between them parenthetical.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذي أَحْسَنَ}: it may follow what precedes it in both the nominative and genitive readings; it may be another khabar; it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; and it may be accusative for praise.
His saying: «خَلَقَه»: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with sukūn on the lām («خَلْقَه»). The others read it with fatḥa. As for the first, it has several analyses. The first: «خَلْقَه» is a badal al-ishtimāl from «كلَّ شيء», and the pronoun returns to «كل شيء». This is the famous, current view. The second: it is a badal al-kull min al-kull (total substitute), and the pronoun on this returns to the Creator the Exalted. The meaning of «أحسن» is «حَسَّن» ("made good"), because there is nothing He created except that it is arranged as wisdom requires, so all creatures are good. The third: «كلَّ شيءٍ» is the first object and «خَلْقَه» the second, with «أحسَنَ» taking on the sense of "gave" and "inspired". Mujāhid said: "He gave every kind its shape." The meaning: He created every thing in its form that He assigned to it. The fourth: «كلَّ شيء» is the second object, fronted, and «خَلْقَه» the first object, postponed, with «أَحْسَنَ» taking on the sense of "inspired" and "made known". Al-Farrāʾ said: "He inspired everything with its creation in what they need, so He made them know that." I say: Abū al-Baqāʾ made «أحسنَ» take the sense of "made known", and parsed it as above, except that the pronoun must be made for Allah the Exalted, and «الخَلْق» made in the sense of «المَخْلوق», that is, "He made His creatures know everything they need", so the meaning comes back to the meaning of His saying {أعطى كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هدى} [Ṭā Hā: 50].
The fifth: the hāʾ returns [to Allah the Exalted] and «خَلْقَه» is accusative as a maṣdar emphasizing the content of the sentence, like His saying {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88]; this is Sībawayh's position, that is, "He created it a creation". It was given preference over badal al-ishtimāl because it contains the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent, which is more frequent than its annexation to the object; and because it is more eloquent as a favour: for when He says {أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} it is more eloquent than «أَحْسَنَ خَلْقَ كلِّ شيء» ("made good the creation of everything"), since the act of creating, which is the attempt, may be good while the thing itself is not good; whereas when He says "He made everything good", it implies that everything He created is good, in the sense that He placed everything in its proper place.
As for the second reading, «خَلَقَ» in it is a past verb, and the sentence is an adjective of the muḍāf or the muḍāf ilayhi, so it is accusative or genitive in position.
His saying: «وَبَدَأ»: the majority read it with the hamza. Al-Zuhrī read «بدا» with a pure alif, which departs from the rule of its softening, since the rule is the intermediate pronunciation (bayna bayna). Although al-Akhfash reported «قَرَيْتُ», the Shaykh allowed it to be from the dialect of the Anṣār. They say «بَدِي» for «بدأ», with kasra on the dāl and a yāʾ after it, as in the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa al-Anṣārī:
3669 - بسمِ الإِلهِ وبه بَدِيْنا ... ولو عَبَدْنا غيرَه شَقِيْنا
(In the name of the Deity and by Him we began; had we worshipped other than Him we would have been wretched.)
He said: "And Ṭayyiʾ say for «بقي», «بَقَا»." He said: "So it is possible that al-Zuhrī's reading is from this dialect, its origin being «بَدِي», then it became «بدا»." I say: then the reading is compounded from two dialects.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ}: this is an iltifāt from the singular third-person pronoun in His saying «نَسْلَه» and on, to the address of a group.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا}: the disagreement of the reciters about the two interrogatives was discussed in Sūrat al-Raʿd. The governing element of «إذا» is omitted, its implied form being "we will be raised" or "we will be brought out", because «خَلْقٍ جديد» points to it. «خَلْق جديد» cannot govern it, because what comes after «إنَّ» and the interrogative does not govern what precedes them. The apodosis of «إذا» is omitted if you take it as conditional.
The majority read «ضَلَلْنا» with dotted ḍād and fatḥa on the lām in the sense of "we disappeared and were lost", from their saying «ضَلَّ اللبنُ في الماء» ("the milk was lost in the water"). It was also said: "we were hidden". Al-Nābigha said:
3670 - فآبَ مُضِلُّوه بعينٍ جَلِيَّة ... وغُوْدِر بالجَوْلانِ حَزْمٌ ونائِلُ
(Those who buried him returned with clear eyes, and prudence and generosity were left behind in al-Jawlān.)
The imperfect of this is «يَضِلُّ» with kasra on the ʿayn, and it is frequent. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū Rajāʾ read it with kasra on the lām, which is the dialect of al-ʿĀliya; the imperfect of this is «يَضَلُّ» with fatḥa. ʿAlī and Abū Ḥaywa read «ضُلِّلْنا» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled kasra-vowelled lām, from «ضَلَّلَه» with doubling.
ʿAlī also, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and Abān ibn Saʿīd read «صَلَلْنا» with undotted ṣād and fatḥa on the lām. And from al-Ḥasan also «صَلِلْنا» with kasra on the ṣād. They are two dialects. It is said «صَلَّ اللحمُ يَصِلُّ» and «يَصَلُّ» with fatḥa or kasra of the ṣād, because the past occurs with fatḥa or kasra on the ʿayn. The meaning of «صَلَّ اللحمُ»: it stank and its smell changed. It is also said «أَصَلَّ» with an alif. He said:
3671 - تُلَجْلِجُ مُضْغَةً فيها أَنِيْضٌ ... أَصَلَّتْ، فَهْيَ تحت الكَشْحِ داءُ
(She rolls a morsel in which there is half-cooked [meat]; it has turned foul, so beneath the flank it is a sickness.)
Al-Naḥḥās said: "We do not know «صَلِلْنا» in the language, but it is said «صَلَّ اللحمُ» and «أصلَّ», and «خَمَّ» and «أَخَمَّ»." Others than Abū Jaʿfar have known it.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {تُرْجَعُونَ}: the majority read it passive. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it active.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَلَوْ ترى}: there are two views on this «لو». The first: it is for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else. Al-Zamakhsharī expressed it as "impossibility because of impossibility", and the Shaykh disputed him on that. Its thorough treatment has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. On this, its apodosis is omitted, that is, "you would have seen a dreadful matter". The second: it is for wishing. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "as if it were said: «وَلَيْتَكَ ترى»." When it is for wishing there is disagreement: does it require an apodosis or not? The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's supposition here is that it has none. The Shaykh said: "The sound view is that it has an apodosis." And he recited the verse of the poet:
3672 - فلو نُبِشَ المقابرُ عن كُلَيْبٍ ... فَيُخبِرَ بالذَّنائبِ أيُّ زِيْرِ
بيومِ الشَّعْثَمَيْنِ لَقَرَّ عيناً ... وكيف لِقاءُ مَنْ تحتَ القُبورِ
(If the graves were dug up for Kulayb, and he were told, by the dhanāʾib, what kind of woman-chaser [Zīr was] on the day of the two Shaʿthams, his eye would be cooled; but how can one under the graves be met?)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لو» comes in the sense of wishing, as you say «لو تأتيني فتحدثَني» just as you say «ليتك تأتيني فتحدثني»." Ibn Mālik said: "If he means by it omission, that is, «وَدِدْتُ لو تأتيني فتحدثَني» ('I wish you would come to me and talk to me'), it is correct; but if he means that it is coined for it, it is not correct; for if it were coined for it, it would not be combined with it, just as «ليت» is not combined with «أتمنى», nor «لعلَّ» with «أترجَّى», nor «إلاَّ» with «أَسْتَثْني». It is permissible to combine «لو» with «أتمنى»: you say «تمنَّيْتُ لو فعلتُ كذا» ('I wished I had done such-and-such')." Is the addressee the Prophet ﷺ or another? There is disagreement. «إذ» is in its usual sense of the past, because «لو» turns the imperfect to the past. It was put in the past here for the certainty of its occurrence, like {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]. Abū al-Baqāʾ made it one of the cases where «إذ» stands in the place of «إذا», and there is no need for it.
His saying: «ناكِسُو»: the majority read it as an active participle annexed to its object for lightness. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَكَسُوا» as a past verb, with «رؤوسَهم» as a direct object.
His saying: «ربَّنا»: on the implication of "saying", and it is a ḥāl, that is, "saying that". Al-Zamakhsharī supposed "they cry for help by their saying", but the implication of "saying" is more frequent.
His saying: «أَبْصَرْنا وسَمِعْنا»: the object may be supposed, that is, "we have seen what we used to deny, and heard what we used to reject"; or it may not be supposed, that is, "we have become seeing and hearing".
His saying: «صالحاً»: it may be a direct object, or an adjective of a maṣdar.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ}: several views are possible in this verse. The first: it is a case of tanāzuʿ (competition), because «ذُوقوا» requires «لقاءَ يومِكم» and «نَسِيْتُمْ» requires it too, that is, "taste the punishment of the meeting of this your Day because you forgot the punishment of the meeting of this your Day"; it is an instance of giving effect to the second according to the Basrans, and to the first according to the Kufans. The first is sounder because of omission from the first; for had the first been given effect, a pronoun would be supplied in the second. The second: the object of «ذُوْقوا» is omitted, that is, "taste the punishment because of your forgetting the meeting of your Day", and «هذا» in these two analyses is an adjective of «يومِكم». The third: the object of «ذوقوا» is «هذا», the pointer referring to the punishment, and the bāʾ is also causal, that is, "so taste this punishment because of your forgetting the meeting of your Day". The apparent sense resists this.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {تتجافى}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, and likewise «يَدْعُون»; if «يَدْعُون» is made a ḥāl it may be a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جُنوبُهم», because the muḍāf is a part. «التجافي» is rising, by which is expressed leaving sleep. Ibn Rawāḥa said:
3673 - نبيٌّ يُجافي جَنْبُه عن فراشِه ... إذا اسْتَثْقَلَتْ بالمشركين المضاجعُ
(A prophet whose side keeps away from his bed when the beds weigh heavy on the polytheists.)
And «خَوْفاً وطَمَعاً»: either an object of purpose, or two ḥāls, or two maṣdars of an implied governing verb.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: «أُخْفِيَ»: Ḥamza read «أُخْفِيْ» as an imperfect verb attributed to the first-person pronoun, hence its yāʾ is sukūn-vowelled because it is nominative [indicative]. The reading of Ibn Masʿūd «ما نُخْفي» with the nūn of majesty supports it. The others read «أُخْفِيَ» as a passive past, hence its yāʾ takes fatḥa. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read «أَخْفى» as an active past, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and the reading of al-Aʿmash «ما أَخْفَيْتُ», attributed to the speaker, supports it. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd], Abū al-Dardāʾ and Abū Hurayra read «مِّن قُرَّاتِ أَعْيُنٍ» in the plural with alif and tāʾ. And «ما» may be relative, that is, "we do not know what Allah has hidden". In the ḥadīth: "What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart of any human." It may also be interrogative, suspending «تَعْلَمُ»; if «تعلم» governs two objects, it fills the place of both, or of one, if one. And «جزاءً» is an object of purpose, or a maṣdar emphasizing the meaning of the sentence before it. When «ما» is interrogative, then in the reading of the one who read what follows it as a past verb, it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the verb after it the khabar; and in the reading of the one who read it as an imperfect, it is a fronted object, and «مِنْ قُرَّة» is a ḥāl from «ما».

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لاَّ يَسْتَوُونَ}: resumptive. It has been reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he used to deliberately pause at His saying «فاسقاً» and then begin «لا يَسْتوون».

semin-durr:19-19.t: Ṭalḥa read «جَنَّةُ المَأْوى» in the singular. The majority read it in the plural. Abū Ḥaywa read «نُزْلاً» with ḍamma and sukūn, and its thorough treatment has preceded at the end of Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {الذي كُنتُمْ بِهِ}: an adjective of «عذابَ». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be an adjective of «النار», saying: it was put in the masculine in the sense of «الجحيم» and «الحريق».

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ}: this [«ثم»] is for the distance between the two ranks in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī likened it to his saying:
367 - 4- وما يَكْشِفُ الغَمَّاءَ إلاَّ ابنُ حُرَّةٍ ... يَرَى غَمَراتِ الموتِ ثم يَزورُها
(None removes the distress except a free-born man, who sees the depths of death and then visits them.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is garbled in the source ("367 - 4-"), probably 3674.] He said: "He deemed it remote that he would visit the depths of death after having seen them, known them and learned of their severity."

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {فِي مِرْيَةٍ}: al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma, and it is a dialect.
His saying: «مِنْ لقائِه»: regarding the hāʾ there are several views. The first: it returns to Mūsā, and the maṣdar is annexed to its object, that is, "from your meeting Mūsā on the night of the Isrāʾ". Al-Mubarrad tested al-Zajjāj on this question and he answered him with what has been mentioned. The second: the pronoun returns to the Book. Then the annexation may be to the agent, that is, "from the Book's meeting Mūsā", or to the object, that is, "from Mūsā's meeting the Book", because the meeting can be attributed to either of them. The third: it returns to the Book, with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "from meeting the like of the Book of Mūsā". The fourth: it returns to the Angel of Death, because of the earlier mention of him. The fifth: it returns to the return, understood from "return" in His saying {إلى رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ}, that is, "do not be in doubt about the meeting of the return". The sixth: it returns to what is understood from the context of the discourse, namely the trial and testing with which Mūsā was afflicted; so said al-Ḥasan, that is, "you must meet what Mūsā met from his people". These are remote views; I mentioned them to point out their weakness. The most apparent: the pronoun is either for Mūsā or for the Book, that is, "do not doubt that Mūsā met the Book and that it was sent down to him".

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {لَمَّا [صَبَرُواْ]}: the two brothers read it with kasra on the lām and a lightened mīm, so that it is the lām of genitive, and «ما» is a maṣdar particle. The prepositional phrase is attached to the making, that is, "We made them so because of their patience and their certainty". The others read it with fatḥa and a doubled mīm. It is the «لمَّا» that requires an apodosis. The two views of Sībawayh and al-Fārisī about it have preceded.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {يُبْصِرُونَ}: the majority read it in the third person; Ibn Masʿūd in the second person as an iltifāt.
«الجُرْز» was also read with sukūn on the rāʾ. It was discussed at the beginning of al-Kahf.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ الفتح}: accusative by «لا يَنْفَعُ», and «لا» does not prevent that. Positions about it have preceded.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {مُّنتَظِرُونَ}: the majority read it with kasra on the ẓāʾ, an active participle. The object of «انتظِرْ» and of «منتظرون» is omitted, that is, "wait for what will befall them; they are waiting, by their own claim, for what will befall you". Al-Yamānī read «مُنْتَظَرُون» as a passive participle.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الم (١) تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢))
His saying (الم): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «تَنْزِيلُ» its khabar (predicate).
التَّنْزِيلُ ("the sending down") has the meaning of الْمُنَزَّلُ ("what is sent down"), and in meaning it is as we mentioned at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Baqara. On this view (لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَابِ, and what governs it is تَنْزِيلُ.
And (مِنْ رَبِّ) is also attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَنْزِيلُ. It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in (فِيهِ), with the adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf) governing it; لَا رَيْبَ here is indeclinable (mabnī).
It is also permissible for (تَنْزِيلُ) to be a mubtadaʾ and «لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ» the khabar, with (مِنْ رَبِّ) a ḥāl as above. On this view (مِنْ) may not be attached to تَنْزِيلُ, because the maṣdar (verbal noun) has already been given a predicate.
It is also permissible for the khabar to be «مِنْ رَبِّ», with «وَلَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ» a ḥāl of الْكِتَابِ; and for it to be a second khabar after a first.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أَتَاهُمْ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ (٣))
His saying (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ): «أَمْ» here is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, i.e. "rather, do they say?" (بَلْ أَيَقُولُونَ).
And «مَا» in «مَا أَتَاهُمْ» is negative, and the statement is a naʿt (adjective) of قَوْمًا.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ (٥))
His saying (مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of أَلْفَ, and it may be a naʿt of سَنَةٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ (٦) الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ طِينٍ (٧))
His saying (الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the one who" (هُوَ الَّذِي), or a second khabar after a first.
[Or] (الْعَزِيزُ) is a mubtadaʾ, «الرَّحِيمُ» a naʿt (adjective), and «الَّذِي» its khabar.
And (خَلْقَهُ) with sukūn on the lām is a badal (substitute) of «كُلَّ», a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "He made excellent the creation of everything".
It may also be a first object (mafʿūl bihi), with «كُلَّ شَيْءٍ» the second, أَحْسَنَ having the meaning of "made known" (عَرَّفَ), i.e. "He made His servants know everything".
It is also read with fatḥa on the lām (خَلَقَهُ), as a past verb; it is then a naʿt of كُلَّ or of شَيْءٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا أَئِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَئِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ بَلْ هُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ كَافِرُونَ (١٠))
His saying (أَئِذَا ضَلَلْنَا): with ḍād, i.e. "we have gone and perished"; and with ṣād (صَلَلْنَا), i.e. "we have become putrid", from your saying صَلَّ اللَّحْمُ, when meat becomes putrid.
What governs «إِذَا» is the meaning of the clause that begins with «إِنَّا», i.e. "when we have perished, shall we be raised?" (إِذَا هَلَكْنَا نُبْعَثُ). «جَدِيدٍ» does not govern it, because what comes after «إِنَّ» does not govern what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ الْمُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ رَبَّنَا أَبْصَرْنَا وَسَمِعْنَا فَارْجِعْنَا نَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ (١٢))
(وَلَوْ تَرَى): it is from seeing with the eye, and the object (mafʿūl bihi) is omitted, i.e. "if you could see the criminals"; the mubtadaʾ (subject) [الْمُجْرِمُونَ] made mentioning it unnecessary. «إِذْ» here refers to the future; we have mentioned the like of this in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. The implied form is "saying: our Lord" (يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا); the position of the omitted element is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is «نَاكِسُوا».

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَذُوقُوا بِمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا إِنَّا نَسِينَاكُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْخُلْدِ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (١٤))
His saying (فَذُوقُوا بِمَا نَسِيتُمْ): i.e. "so taste the punishment". It is also permissible for the object (mafʿūl bihi) of «فَذُوقُوا» to be «لِقَاءَ», according to the view of the Kufans in letting the first [of two competing verbs] govern; and it is permissible for the object of «ذُوقُوا» to be «هَذَا», i.e. "this punishment".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ (١٦))
His saying (تَتَجَافَى) and (يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ): they are in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا) has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٧))
His saying (مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ): «مَا» may be an interrogative, its position being the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ» its khabar (predicate), according to the reading of those who put fatḥa on the yāʾ. According to the reading of those who put sukūn on it (أُخْفِي) and make it the imperfect "I hide", «مَا» is in the position of the accusative, governed by أُخْفِي.
It is also permissible for «مَا» to have the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which"), in the accusative, governed by تَعْلَمُ.
And (مِنْ قُرَّةِ), on both views, is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «أُخْفِيَ».
And (جَزَاءً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they were recompensed with a recompense" (جُوزُوا جَزَاءً).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَنْ كَانَ فَاسِقًا لَا يَسْتَوُونَ (١٨))
His saying (لَا يَسْتَوُونَ): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf) and has no grammatical position, and it has the meaning of the implied sense mentioned above. And (نُزُلًا) has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا فَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ كُلَّمَا أَرَادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا أُعِيدُوا فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ النَّارِ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ (٢٠))
His saying (الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ): it is a naʿt (adjective) of الْعَذَابِ, in the position of the accusative.
It may also be a naʿt of النَّارِ, put in the masculine on the sense of الْجَحِيم ("Hellfire") or الْحَرِيق ("the burning").

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: {وَلَقَد آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكتاب فَلَا تكن فِي مرية من لِقَائِه وجعلناه هدى لبني إِسْرَائِيل}
His saying (مِنْ لِقَائِهِ): the hāʾ may be the pronoun of the name of Allah, i.e. "of Moses' meeting Allah", so the maṣdar (verbal noun) is in genitive construct with its object; and it may be the pronoun of Moses, so that it is in genitive construct with its agent.
It is also said: it refers back to the Book, as Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ).
It is also said: [it means] "of your meeting, O Muḥammad, Moses" — may Allah bless them both and grant them peace — on the night of the Ascension (al-Miʿrāj).

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا وَكَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ (٢٤))
(لَمَّا) with shadda is an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «جَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ» or يَهْدُونَ. And with the lightened form and kasra on the lām (لِمَا), on the basis that it [مَا] is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ أَفَلَا يَسْمَعُونَ (٢٦))
(كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Ṭā Hā.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Sajda
Meccan,
except for three verses of it which are Medinan: ﴿أفَمَن كانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كانَ فاسِقًا﴾ [al-Sajda: 18], to the end of the three verses.
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلُ الكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Sajda: 2] — Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related, with a chain of transmission of his, «that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite every night Sūrat al-Sajda, "Alif Lām Mīm, Tanzīl," and Sūrat "Tabārak," al-Mulk». And Kaʿb al-Aḥbār related that he said: «"Whoever recites Sūrat al-Sajda, seventy good deeds are written for him, seventy evil deeds are removed from him, and he is raised seventy degrees."»
His saying: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Sajda: 2] — we have explained what has been said about ”الـم“. ”تَنْزِيلُ“ is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the implied form "What we recite is the sending down of the Book." It may also be, in meaning, a khabar about ”الـم“, i.e. "Alif Lām Mīm is of the sending down of the Book." And it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar of the mubtadaʾ being ”لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ“.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالُوا أإذا ضَلَلْنا في الأرْضِ أإنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ — and it is read ”أنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, and it is read ”إنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“. The position of ”إذا“ is accusative. Whoever reads ”أئِنّا“, it is in the sense of "Shall we be resurrected when we are lost in the earth?!", and ”إنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“ indicates it. Whoever reads ”إنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, then ”إذا“ is accusative by ”ضَلَلْنا“, and it is in the sense of condition and recompense; and it does no harm that the fāʾ is not mentioned, because ”إذا“ has been followed by a past verb. It is not permissible for ”إذا“ to be made accusative by what comes after ”إنَّ“; there is no disagreement among the grammarians about that. The meaning of ”إذا ضَلَلْنا“ is: "when we have died and become dust and bones, and are lost in the earth, so that nothing of our form is discernible." And it is read ”صَلَلْنا“, with ṣād, and its meaning is of two kinds. One of them: "we have rotted and changed, and our forms have changed"; one says ”صَلَّ اللَّحْمُ“ and ”أصَلَّ“ when meat rots and changes. The second kind: ”صَلَلْنا“: we have become of the kind of al-ṣalla, which is dry earth.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ يَتَوَفّاكم مَلَكُ المَوْتِ﴾ — from paying a number in full; its interpretation is that he takes all your souls, so that not one of you is missing, as you say "I have received in full from so-and-so" and "I have received in full from so-and-so my property that was with him," whose interpretation is that nothing remains owed to me by him.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ ناكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — this has its apodosis (jawāb) left out. The address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to creation; the proof of that is ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. So it is equivalent to "if you (plural) were to see," and the apodosis is: "you would see that from which the utmost lesson is to be taken."
His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا أبْصَرْنا وسَمِعْنا﴾ — there is an implied "they say" in it: "they say: Our Lord, we have seen."

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا لآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُداها﴾ — its interpretation is like His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهم عَلى الهُدى﴾ [al-Anʿām: 35], and similar to it is: ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 4].
His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ حَقَّ القَوْلُ مِنِّي لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الجِنَّةِ والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾ — Qatāda said: on account of their sins. And this is good, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 16].

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿فَذُوقُوا بِما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكم هَذا إنّا نَسِيناكُمْ﴾ — the interpretation of forgetting here is abandoning. The meaning is: "So taste, because you abandoned working for the meeting of this Day of yours; so We have abandoned you [and kept you] from mercy."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَتَجافى جُنُوبُهم عَنِ المَضاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهم خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا﴾ — the meaning of ”تَتَجافى“ is: they rise and leave their beds. The meaning of ”خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا“ is: in fear of Allah's punishment and in hope of Allah's mercy. ”خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا“ are accusative because they are mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), as you say ”فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ حِذارَ الشَّرِّ“ (I did that in wariness of evil), i.e. for wariness of evil. Its reality is that it is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun), because "they call upon their Lord" in this place indicates that they fear His punishment and hope for His mercy; so it is in the interpretation of "they fear with fear and hope with hope."
His saying: ﴿وَمِمّا رَزَقْناهم يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ — i.e. they spend in obedience to Allah. There has been disagreement about its interpretation, and most of what has come in the tafsīr is that they used to pray at night at the time of the prescribed ʿatama (night) prayer, not sleeping through it. And it has been said: the voluntary prayer between the two prayers — the sunset prayer and the late-evening prayer.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهم مِن قُرَّةِ أعْيُنٍ﴾ — is proof that it is the prayer in the depth of the night, because it is a deed which a person does in secret; so He made the wording of what it is rewarded with ”أُخْفِيَ“ (has been hidden). And it is read with the yāʾ vowelless, and the meaning is "what I hide for them" — a report from Allah [about Himself]. When it is read ”أُخْفِيَ لَهم مِن قُرَّةِ أعْيُنٍ“ — with fatḥa on the yāʾ — it is in the interpretation of the past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is what is in ”أُخْفِيَ“ referring to ”ما“. All the people read ”مِن قُرَّةِ أعْيُنٍ“ except Abū Hurayra, who read ”مِن قُرّاتِ أعْيُنٍ“ and related it from the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — ”جَزاءً“ is also accusative, a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). And it has been read ”فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أخْفى لَهم“, i.e. "what Allah has hidden for them."

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿أفَمَن كانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كانَ فاسِقًا لا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr that it was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ: the believer is ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and the transgressor is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. So Allah testified for ʿAlī to faith, and that he is in Paradise, by His saying: ﴿أمّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَلَهم جَنّاتُ المَأْوى﴾ [al-Sajda: 19]. He said ”لا يَسْتَوُونَ“ (they are not equal, plural); had He said ”لا يَسْتَوِيانِ“ (dual), it would have been permissible. But ”مَن“ has the wording of a singular while indicating both the singular and the plural; so ”لا يَسْتَوُونَ“ came in the sense of "the believers and the unbelievers are not equal." It is also possible that ”لا يَسْتَوُونَ“ is for the two, because the meaning of two is a plurality.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهم مِنَ العَذابِ الأدْنى دُونَ العَذابِ الأكْبَرِ﴾ — ”اَلْأدْنى“ (the nearer) is what befalls them in this world. There has been disagreement about its interpretation. It has been said: what befalls them of drought and fear; and the proof of this view is His saying: ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكم بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الخَوْفِ والجُوعِ ونَقْصٍ مِنَ الأمْوالِ والأنْفُسِ والثَّمَراتِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 155]. And it has been said: ”اَلْعَذابُ الأدْنى“ here is captivity and killing. In sum, everything with which one is punished in this world is the nearer punishment, and the greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ فَلا تَكُنْ في مِرْيَةٍ مِن لِقائِهِ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr: "Do not be in doubt about meeting Mūsā, upon him be peace"; and the proof of this view in the tafsīr is His saying: ﴿واسْألْ مَن أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُسُلِنا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]. So the meaning is: "Do not be, O Muḥammad, in doubt about meeting him." The address to the Prophet ﷺ is equivalent to an address to him and his community in this place, i.e. "so do not be in doubt about the Prophet's meeting, upon him be peace, with Mūsā." And it has been said: ”فَلا تَكُنْ في مِرْيَةٍ مِن لِقائِهِ“ means "of Mūsā's receiving the Book," so the hāʾ is for the Book, and in "his meeting" there is a reference to Mūsā. And it is possible that the hāʾ is for Mūsā and the Book is omitted, because the Book has been mentioned just as Mūsā has been mentioned; and this — and Allah knows best — is closer to the tafsīr.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِنهم أئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأمْرِنا﴾ — most of the Basrans do not permit ”أئِمَّةً“ with two hamzas; Ibn Abī Isḥāq alone permits the combination of two hamzas. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans — except Ibn [Abī] Isḥāq — say ”أيِمَّةً“, with a hamza and a yāʾ; when the two hamzas are in one word they permit nothing but replacing the second, as in ”أيِمَّةً“ and ”آدَمَ“. Whoever reads ”أئِمَّةً“ is obliged to say for ”آدَمَ“ ”أأْدَمَ“, because it is [the pattern] ”أفْعَلُ“ from ”اَلْأُدْمَةُ“ (brownness), and ”أئِمَّةً“ is ”أفْعِلَةً“. It ought not to be read except as ”أيِمَّةً“, because whoever pronounces the hamza fully where lightening of the hamza is permissible [also] permits the lightening; so likewise he permits the lightening in ”أيِمَّةً“, and the reading ”أيِمَّةً“ thus becomes a matter of consensus.
His saying: ﴿لَمّا صَبَرُوا﴾, and ”لِما صَبَرُوا“ — the reading is with doubling and without doubling in ”لَمّا“. Without doubling, the meaning is: "We made them leaders because of their patience." Whoever reads ”لَمّا صَبَرُوا“, the meaning is that of recounting a recompense: "When they were patient, We made them leaders." The basis of the recompense in this is as though it had been said: "If you are patient, We will make you leaders; so when they were patient they were made leaders."

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهم كَمْ أهْلَكْنا﴾ — and it has been read with nūn: ”أوَلَمْ نَهْدِ لَهم“. One of the grammarians claimed that ”كَمْ“ is in the position of the nominative by ”يَهْدِ“, the meaning according to him being: "Have We not made clear to them the generations that We destroyed before them?!" This in our view — I mean in the view of the Basrans — is not permissible, because it makes what is before ”كَمْ“ govern ”كَمْ“. It is not permissible, in your saying ”كَمْ رَجُلٍ جاءَنِي“ (how many a man came to me!) when you are making a statement, to say ”جاءَنِي كَمْ رَجُلٍ“, because ”كَمْ“ is never moved from the initial position. For that reason it is permitted to separate it from what it governs when it is put in the accusative, in both the declarative and the interrogative [use]. You say in the declarative: ”كَمْ بِجُودٍ مُقْرِفًا نالَ الغِنى“ (how many a base-born man has attained riches through generosity!).
So you separated ”كَمْ“ from your saying ”مُقْرِفًا“ by your saying ”بِجُودٍ“; the separation in it between ”كَمْ“ and what it governs is a compensation for its [lack of] flexibility. Do you not see that ”عِشْرُونَ عِنْدِي دِرْهَمًا“ (twenty I have dirhams) is not permissible? Yet in the declarative ”كَمْ عِنْدِي دِرْهَمًا جَيِّدًا“ is permissible. The truth of this is that ”كَمْ“ is in the position of the accusative by ”أهْلَكْنا“, and the fāʿil (agent) of ”يَهْدِ“ is what the meaning indicates from the preceding speech; ”كَمْ“ is also an indication of the agent in ”يَهْدِي“.
