What indicates this is the reading of whoever read ”أوَلَمْ نَهْدِ“, with nūn, i.e. "Have We not made clear to them?!" It is also possible, with ”يَهْدِ“ with yāʾ, that the verb is Allah's, Mighty and Majestic is He; the reading of whoever read ”أوَلَمْ نَهْدِ“ indicates this.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنّا نَسُوقُ الماءَ إلى الأرْضِ الجُرُزِ فَنُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا تَأْكُلُ مِنهُ أنْعامُهم وأنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ — it is read ”اَلْجُرُزِ“, and ”اَلْجَرَزِ“, ”اَلْجُرْزِ“ and ”اَلْجَرْزِ“ are permissible; all of that has been reported for ”اَلْجُرُزِ“. It has come in the tafsīr that it is the land of Yemen. ”اَلْجُرُزُ“ according to the people of the language is land that does not put forth vegetation; its origin was that it eats up its vegetation. One says ”اِمْرَأةٌ جَرُوزٌ“ when a woman is a big eater, and one says ”سَيْفٌ جُرازٌ“ when a sword cuts off at the root. Whoever says ”جُرْزٌ“, it is a lightening of ”جُرُزٌ“; and whoever says ”جَرَزٌ“ and ”جَرْزٌ“, they are two dialect forms. It is also possible that ”جَرْزٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, as though it is land possessed of jarz — I mean with sukūn on the rāʾ — i.e. possessed of the eating up of vegetation.
His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ في مَساكِنِهِمْ﴾ [al-Sajda: 26] — in ”يَمْشُونَ في مَساكِنِهِمْ“, ”تَمْشُونَ“ (you walk) is permissible.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هَذا الفَتْحُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr that the Companions of the Prophet, upon him be peace, said: "Soon there will be for us a day on which we have rest." So the idolaters said: "When is this victory (fatḥ), if you are truthful?!" Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that rest is in Paradise, in the Hereafter. It has also come concerning al-fatḥ: "When is this judgement, if you are truthful?!" and "When is this decision?!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that on the Day of Decision (fatḥ) the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be granted respite; i.e. as long as they are in this world, repentance is offered to them, but there is no repentance in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾ — its meaning is: "Rather, do they say: he invented it?"
His saying: ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا ما أتاهم مِن نَذِيرٍ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — and similar to it is ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا ما أُنْذِرَ آباؤُهُمْ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 6]. ”ما“ in both places is negation, i.e. neither they nor their fathers witnessed a prophet. As for the warning by the earlier messengers of Allah, Allah's blessings be upon them, the proof is established against their fathers through it, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, punishes only whoever disbelieves in the messengers; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 15].

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهم وانْتَظِرْ إنَّهم مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ — and it has been read ”فانْتَظِرْ إنَّهم مُنْتَظِرُونَ“, and ”مُنْتَظَرُونَ“ (they are awaited).

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إلَيْهِ في يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ ألْفَ سَنَةٍ مِمّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, then the affair ascends to Him in a day, and that day's measure is a thousand years of what you count. The meaning of ”يَعْرُجُ“ is: descends and ascends [Translator's note: so in the source, «يَنْزِلُ، ويَصْعَدُ»]. One says ”عَرَجْتُ في السُّلَّمِ، أعْرُجُ“ (I climbed the ladder), and one says ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرُجُ“ when one becomes lame.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الَّذِي أحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾ — it has been read ”خَلَقَهُ“ both with a vowel on the lām and with sukūn on it; and ”خَلْقُهُ“, in the nominative, is permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read it. As for ”خَلَقَهُ“, it is as the past verb; and the interpretation of "making good" in this is that He created it according to His will: He created the human being in the finest stature, and He created the ape as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, wished, and His creating it thus is of the most consummate wisdom. Whoever reads ”خَلْقَهُ“, with sukūn on the lām, it is in two ways: one of them is as the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by ”أحْسَنَ“, the meaning being "He who created everything, a creating of it"; and it may be as a badal (substitute), so the meaning would be "He who made good the creation of everything, its creation." The nominative is with the implied form "that is His creation."
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَدَأ خَلْقَ الإنْسانِ مِن طِينٍ﴾ — He means Adam and his offspring; for Adam was created from clay.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُ مِن سُلالَةٍ مِن ماءٍ مَهِينٍ﴾ — the meaning of ”مَهِينٍ“ is: weak. The meaning of ”اَلسُّلالَةُ“ in the language is the small amount that slips out of a thing; and likewise [the pattern] ”اَلْفُعالَةُ“, such as ”اَلْفُضالَةُ“ (leftover), ”اَلنُّخامَةُ“ (phlegm) and ”اَلْقُوارَةُ“ (cut-off piece).
